item.title: I’m sorry, but I thought Notre Dame was supposed to JOIN A CONFERENCE
item.description: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - DECEMBER 19: Quarterback Ian Book #12 of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish warms up on the sideline in the first half against the Clemson Tigers during the ACC Championship game at Bank of America Stadium on December 19, 2020 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s practically a battle cry across college football whenever anyone invokes the name of Notre Dame. JOIN A CONFERENCE Outside of it being annoying and completely ignorant of Notre Dame’s history, and in some ways the history of college football, the phrase itself might be history as well. The impending expansion of the college football playoff to 24 teams is making some major waves in the sport as the system is changing course. Once the new 24 team playoff is in place, there will be NO more conference championship games. So, essentially, conferences are just scheduling partners with group media rights. That’s exactly as lame as it sounds. In a 18 team or 20 team conference, who in the hell is the true conference champion without some wild tiebreakers or just the luck of the scheduling draw? And again… who really cares when there is a massive national playoff on tap? There really is no point. The Miami Hurricanes are quickly coming to this realization. In the "second tier" of college sports' caste system, Miami is positioning itself for a conference move while exploring football independence and fighting against a federal bill. "If we have to go independent," the president says, "I like our chances." https://t.co/AGBdulm1OU — Ross Dellenger (@RossDellenger) October 22, 2026 The Canes, like Florida State and Clemson, are feeling the squeeze of being members of the ACC — a “second tier” conference according to some. They’re looking for a way out, and that way out could be independence. “If we have to go independent, I like our chances because we are a national brand. I wouldn’t like to do that because scheduling [other sports] is really tough. It’s great for football but what about track, volleyball and the golf team?” There really is no way of knowing what moves these schools will eventually make (if any) but it’s becoming clearer and clearer, that being in a conference (top tier or not) isn’t anything close to what it used to be. The program who is best suited to move forward in this new era is seemingly the Notre Dame Fighting Irish — who have been independent since day one. Join a conference. Why? What’s the point? What difference would any of it make as we get into 2027? You’re right… pretty much none. If the entire world of college football has come down to maximizing football revenue and the playoff, it makes little sense to tie oneself to a group of schools just get a conference Boy Scout Patch on the uniform. Independence yesterday. Independence today. Independence forever for Notre Dame, and maybe a few other programs finally figure it out.

item.title: Michael Carrick blamed for Bruno Fernandes tactical mutiny after failing to discipline Lisandro Martinez at Manchester United
item.description: Former Premier League striker Troy Deeney believes Manchester United boss Michael Carrick invited Bruno Fernandes' recent tactical criticism by failing to drop Lisandro Martinez last week. The Old Trafford skipper publicly questioned his manager's approach following Wednesday's humbling 4-1 Champions League defeat away at Como. Lenient management sparks captain outburst Carrick has been accused of undermining his own authority in the Red Devils dressing room by letting Martinez go unpunished before Fernandes criticised his game plan in Italy . Following the midweek rout, the Portuguese midfielder claimed the team needed to be "more brave under pressure" and "take the risk of pressing high". However, his boss argued that a lack of running caused the defeat rather than tactics. Pundit blasts weak disciplinary stance imago-sport-1058429966.jpg Fernandes' public complaints arrived just days after Martinez called out technical director Jason Wilcox for failing to properly reinforce the squad during the summer transfer window. Although the Argentine centre-back subsequently apologised for those remarks , he avoided a suspension and started last Sunday's 1-1 draw against Leeds United at Elland Road. Speaking on Premier League All Access , former Watford striker Deeney insisted that retaining the defender inadvertently emboldened the club captain to speak out of turn: "Last week when Martinez said what he said, you can't let him play. You've got to nip that in the bud and just be like, 'I get you apologising and all of that, but, you're out of the team this week.' And I know he probably looked around and went, 'I haven't got much here, I haven't got much in the way of help, we're at Elland Road.' You need to nip it in the bud. "The second he didn't and Martinez played, he inadvertently allows for Bruno Fernandes to talk. Bruno Fernandes feeds it to the open season, 'I can say what I want.' But Bruno Fernandes, I've been saying this for three years, when he hasn't got the goals or assists, he's not a captain. We've had this discussion so many times, he's not a leader." Boardroom anger fuels toxic mood While the manager and his skipper must quickly resolve their differences to halt a dismal seven-game winless streak, supporters are increasingly directing their fury towards the Old Trafford hierarchy. Assessing the mood among the fanbase ahead of Sunday's return to domestic action, talkSPORT chief football correspondent Alex Crook warned that the stadium atmosphere could 'turn quite toxic' if results do not improve immediately: "I think there were a lot of angry Manchester United fans, both inside the stands and watching at home in midweek. "They'll have seen what Bruno Fernandes has said. They'll feel for Michael Carrick. I think they do feel empathy for Michael Carrick. He's a club legend, someone who won the European Cup as a player. Someone who stepped in in their hour of need last season. "They are very angry with those above Carrick, the likes of Jaso

Bournemouth have the capability to run all over Manchester United." The Cherries arrive in Manchester full of confidence after following up their 2-0 league win over Sunderland with a sensational 3-0 Europa League demolition of AC Milan . For Carrick and his players, avoiding an early setback will be crucial to prevent mounting frustration in the stands from escalating.

item.title: App State spoils James Madison’s perfect season, 34-31 in OT
item.description: BOONE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 22: Appalachian State Mountaineers fans storm the field after a 34-31 win against the James Madison Dukes at Kidd Brewer Stadium on October 22, 2026 in Boone, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s something about a fall weeknight in Boone, NC. The air is crisper. The foliage more scenic. The black and gold striped overalls more abundant. And the upsets are riper for the picking. James Madison entered the environment Thursday night as one of six remaining undefeated FBS teams. It left blemished, stunned by an Appalachian State team that utilized its homefield advantage to overcome a double-digit deficit and emerge victorious in overtime, 34-31. The Mountaineer fans stood anxiously, wondering if the upset opportunity passed them by. On the final drive of regulation, a trailing James Madison converted two fourth downs by the skin of its teeth. Then with eight seconds remaining, the Dukes snapped the ball from the 6-yard line, and quarterback Camden Coleman found a free running lane to the end zone, knotting the game at 31-31. App State won the overtime coin toss, decided to defend first, and the conditions for an upset strengthened on the first play of the extra period. James Madison attempted a trick play, placing running back Seth Cromwell behind the center in shotgun formation. Cromwell fielded a direct snap and handed the ball off to quarterback JC Evans. Before the quarterback could survey downfield, App State’s nickel corner Ja’Den McBurrows already met Evans in the backfield, tripping him 11 yards behind the line of scrimmage. The Dukes never returned to the original line of scrimmage, and on 4th-and-14, Morgan Suarez’s 47-yard field goal attempt collided with the left upright, leaving the door wide open for an upset. App State’s offense didn’t need to travel far in overtime. Instead, the Mountaineers trusted their kicker. They sent James London onto the field on 3rd-and-7 to deliver the game-winner, and the 40-yard attempt sailed through the uprights, initiating a field storm at Kidd-Brewer Stadium. Long before the field storm, App State found itself trailing 14-3 in the second quarter. But a methodical 10-play, 75-yard touchdown drive, ending in an Alexander Sanchez touchdown reception, thinned the deficit to 14-10 at halftime. item.content:encoded: BOONE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 22: Appalachian State Mountaineers fans storm the field after a 34-31 win against the James Madison Dukes at Kidd Brewer Stadium on October 22, 2026 in Boone, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s something about a fall weeknight in Boone, NC. The air is crisper. The foliage more scenic. The black and gold striped overalls more abundant. And the upsets are riper for the picking. James Madison entered the environment Thursday night as one of six remaining undefeated FBS teams. It left blemished, stunned by an Appalachian State team that utilized its homefield advantage to overcome a double-digit deficit and emerge victorious in overtime, 34-31. The Mountaineer fans stood anxiously, wondering if the upset opportunity passed them by. On the final drive of regulation, a trailing James Madison converted two fourth downs by the skin of its teeth. Then with eight seconds remaining, the Dukes snapped the ball from the 6-yard line, and quarterback Camden Coleman found a free running lane to the end zone, knotting the game at 31-31. App State won the overtime coin toss, decided to defend first, and the conditions for an upset strengthened on the first play of the extra period. James Madison attempted a trick play, placing running back Seth Cromwell behind the center in shotgun formation. Cromwell fielded a direct snap and handed the ball off to quarterback JC Evans. Before the quarterback could survey downfield, App State’s nickel corner Ja’Den McBurrows already met Evans in the backfield, tripping him 11 yards behind the line of scrimmage. The Dukes never returned to the original line of scrimmage, and on 4th-and-14, Morgan Suarez’s 47-yard field goal attempt collided with the left upright, leaving the door wide open for an upset. App State’s offense didn’t need to travel far in overtime. Instead, the Mountaineers trusted their kicker. They sent James London onto the field on 3rd-and-7 to deliver the game-winner, and the 40-yard attempt sailed through the uprights, initiating a field storm at Kidd-Brewer Stadium. Long before the field storm, App State found itself trailing 14-3 in the second quarter. But a methodical 10-play, 75-yard touchdown drive, ending in an Alexander Sanchez touchdown reception, thinned the deficit to 14-10 at halftime. That generated the momentum the Mountaineer offense needed to compete in the second half. They further cut the deficit to 14-13 on the opening drive of the second half, and then they knotted it at 21-21 on a Malachi Singleton to Chris Lofton connection and a 2-point conversion. After the teams traded field goals, App State finally recorded the breakthrough play it needed to put JMU on alert. With roughly six minutes remaining in a 24-24 ballgame, middle linebacker Colton Phares sat in front of a route, intercepting Coleman and returning the ball to the JMU 14-yard line. A pass interference set Hasselbeck for another touchdown strike, this time to tight end Luke Douglas for the lead. Although James Madison tied it up on a gutsy final drive — despite losing star running back George Pettaway to injury in the process — the Mountaineers prevailed in overtime, just like they did against the Dukes in 2023. In fact, Thursday night marked James Madison’s sixth Sun Belt defeat since 2023, and it was the third in overtime fashion. This Sun Belt East matchup was particularly unique as both teams deployed two-quarterback systems. App State used Singleton as the primary option but inserted Hasselbeck for certain packages. The two combined to finish 29-of-44 with 285 yards passing and three touchdowns without an interception. Meanwhile, James Madison alternated Coleman and Evans, who collectively threw for 331 yards on a 27-of-46 showing, complete with two touchdowns and an interception. The offenses were similar in other respects, too. Neither team had consistent success running the ball, and both passing attacks distributed the wealth evenly. Nine Mountaineers caught a pass, as did 10 Dukes. No player finished with more than six catches or 84 receiving yards in a game defined by quarterback production. One striking difference between the Sun Belt opponents was special teams. James Madison finished 1-of-3 on field goals, while London sunk all four of his attempts for App State, including the 40-yard game-winner. London’s field goal jumpstarted a black and gold celebration at midfield, representing a rebirth for App State football. The program was fresh off its first two losing seasons since joining the FBS in 2014, and now, it stands one win away from returning to bowl eligibility. Second-year head coach Dowell Loggains secured his signature victory Thursday, as App State improved to 5-2 overall and 2-1 in Sun Belt play. On the flipside, head coach Billy Napier suffered his first defeat at James Madison. Napier fell to 32-8 all-time against Sun Belt opponents, and five of those eight defeats were to App State. The Dukes are no longer perfect, snapping a 17-game regular season win streak. While the window remains open, James Madison’s chances of a second-straight College Football Playoff appearance took a significant hit Thursday night in Boone.

item.title: Exeter's Wyatt suffers fresh injury blow
item.description: Tommy Wyatt has made four starts in all competitions for Exeter this season [Shutterstock] Exeter back Tommy Wyatt could be out until December after injuring his ankle. It is the latest problem for the 26-year-old, who returned from a serious knee injury this summer, only to damage his shoulder in the final game of pre-season. Wyatt came off in the first half of Exeter's European Champions Cup loss at Toulouse having played Exeter's previous three games. It add more pressure to Exeter's strained backs division ahead of Saturday's Prem game at Bristol (17:30 BST). Winger Campbell Ridl is out for the season, England's Immanuel Feyi-Waboso has a hamstring issue while Paul Brown-Bampoe and Olly Woodburn are also injured. "The initial prognosis is it's not operable," Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter told BBC Sport. "So he should be back either late in the Prem Cup period or as we get back into the Premiership hopefully if things go well. "It was another significant injury to a back three player which we seem to be we seem to be stacking up pretty quickly. "You've got to feel for him, but it's part of the game now and you've kind of got to get on with it."

item.title: Today's 5 headlines: Clásico preview; Spanish wins in Europe
item.description: Today's 5 headlines: Clásico preview; Spanish wins in Europe Good morning and happy Friday. Yesterday brought the European and South American international action to a close. Here are the day's top 5 stories to keep you up to date with the football world. The build-up to El Clásico is heating up Real Madrid face a crucial LaLiga clash this Sunday when they visit Spotify Camp Nou. Los Blancos head into the big game in peak form after rounding off a perfect week in European competition. The mood in the opposing camp is very different following their European setback. FC Barcelona go into the clash with defensive concerns after suffering a heavy 4-2 defeat away to Paris Saint-Germain. Barça have won every home game since November 2025; Real Madrid, coming off four straight wins, are looking to end their rivals' home dominance. Real Sociedad and Celta win in the Europa League Last night was a glorious one for the Spanish sides in the Europa League. Both teams secured their first wins in international competition and are dreaming of going further in the tournament. Matarazzo's side showed their quality by thrashing Norway's Lillestrom 6-0 away, putting the game to bed in the first half thanks to a hat-trick of assists from Mikel Oyarzabal and goals from Sergio Gómez and Luka Sucic. Celta secured a valuable European victory after coming from behind to beat Celtic 2-1 away in Glasgow. Although the Scottish side took the lead through Mika Baur early in the second half, a brilliant brace from Javi Rodríguez turned the game around and sealed the first continental win for Claudio Giráldez's team. Estudiantes beat Flamengo to reach the Copa Libertadores final Estudiantes de La Plata beat the Brazilian side in a penalty shootout (2-3) and will play in the final on November 28 at the Estadio Centenario in Montevideo. 📸 Buda Mendes - 2026 Getty Images After holding out for more than 40 minutes with ten men following Baltasar Rodríguez's sending-off in a tense 0-0 draw, Fernando Muslera stood tall in the shootout, saving three crucial penalties from Jorginho, Lucas Paquetá and Bruno Henrique. European surprises: Milan and Juve stumble; Benfica and Leverkusen deliver Elsewhere in Europe, the heavy defeats of continental giants stood out, with AC Milan thrashed 3-0 by Bournemouth and Olympique Lyonnais also suffering a resounding 3-0 loss to Hoffenheim. Meanwhile, Juventus could only draw 2-2 at home to Rennes and Beşiktaş drew 2-2 with Crystal Palace, while Bayer Leverkusen, who won 2-0 at OFI Crete, and Benfica, who thrashed Omonia Nicosia 4-1 away, were among the night's success stories. item.title: AC Milan renew interest in Real Madrid forward but receive clear response from the club – report
item.description: AC Milan renew interest in Real Madrid forward but receive clear response from the club – report Real Madrid and Endrick have rejected an approach from AC Milan over a potential move for the Brazilian forward, according to Bernabeu Digital . As per the outlet, the Italian club renewed its interest in the youngster around a month ago, but neither the player nor the Spanish giants is currently willing to consider a transfer. Milan have continued to monitor Endrick’s situation in Madrid, hoping to explore the possibility of bringing him to Serie A. Their latest inquiry, though, has not changed the player’s position or the club’s plans. Milan renew interest but Real Madrid refuse to entertain a move Endrick has attracted interest from Milan before , although Real Madrid have been clear that they have no intention of letting the forward leave, while the Brazilian also remains determined to establish himself in Spain. AC Milan have renewed their interest in Endrick. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Notably, the renewed inquiry did not develop into negotiations because neither side was prepared to move forward. Rather, Milan’s interest should be viewed as an attempt to assess the situation rather than evidence that a transfer is close. Endrick determined to succeed at Real Madrid The Brazilian faces significant competition for attacking places at Real Madrid, making regular minutes difficult to secure. Breaking into the first team requires him to compete with established players while adapting to the demands and expectations of one of Europe’s biggest clubs. Endrick does not want to leave Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Despite that challenge, Endrick believes his future remains at the Bernabeu . He is not convinced that moving to Italian football would be the right decision at this stage of his career, and Real Madrid also view him as a player with considerable room for development. That position matters because a lack of playing time does not automatically mean a player wants to leave. Endrick’s immediate priority is to earn more opportunities within the existing setup rather than pursue a fresh start elsewhere.

Milan renew interest but Real Madrid refuse to entertain a move Endrick has attracted interest from Milan before , although Real Madrid have been clear that they have no intention of letting the forward leave, while the Brazilian also remains determined to establish himself in Spain. AC Milan have renewed their interest in Endrick. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Notably, the renewed inquiry did not develop into negotiations because neither side was prepared to move forward. Rather, Milan’s interest should be viewed as an attempt to assess the situation rather than evidence that a transfer is close. Endrick determined to succeed at Real Madrid The Brazilian faces significant competition for attacking places at Real Madrid, making regular minutes difficult to secure. Breaking into the first team requires him to compete with established players while adapting to the demands and expectations of one of Europe’s biggest clubs. Endrick does not want to leave Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Despite that challenge, Endrick believes his future remains at the Bernabeu . He is not convinced that moving to Italian football would be the right decision at this stage of his career, and Real Madrid also view him as a player with considerable room for development. That position matters because a lack of playing time does not automatically mean a player wants to leave. Endrick’s immediate priority is to earn more opportunities within the existing setup rather than pursue a fresh start elsewhere.

item.title: Barcelona consider Sergio Busquets for future coaching role after Hansi Flick – report
item.description: Barcelona consider Sergio Busquets for future coaching role after Hansi Flick – report Barcelona are keeping a close eye on Sergio Busquets’ development as a coach, with the former midfielder emerging as a potential candidate for an important role at the club. Hansi Flick is currently leading the first team with some style, and his project very much seems to be in its early stages as things stand. However, according to SPORT , Barcelona’s sporting department views Busquets as someone with the potential to take on greater responsibilities in the future. Busquets begins his coaching journey at Barcelona The former Barcelona captain is currently gaining coaching experience with the club’s reserve team, working alongside Juliano Belletti. The arrangement allows Busquets to develop his understanding of coaching while remaining connected to the environment where he spent the majority of his playing career. Sergio Busquets is learning the trade from Juliano Belletti. (Photo courtesy: FC Barcelona official website) Barcelona believe his background and knowledge of the club could make him an interesting option for future responsibilities. The club are also monitoring former midfielder Cesc Fabregas, whose impressive work at Como has placed him among the possible candidates to eventually succeed Flick. However, neither candidate has been designated as the German coach’s replacement, and it is too early to be having those conversations. Why Busquets could be an interesting option for Barcelona Few former players understand Barcelona’s footballing identity as deeply as Busquets. During his playing career, he was central to the team’s positional structure, controlling possession, anticipating danger and helping team-mates find space. His understanding of positioning and midfield organisation would be particularly valuable in a club that continues to place considerable importance on technical intelligence. Barcelona are making plans for life after Hansi Flick. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) There is also precedent. In many ways, Busquets was a very similar player to Pep Guardiola and could look to follow the same path. There is also an emotional dimension to the possibility of Busquets eventually taking on a prominent coaching role . Having a former captain involved in shaping Barcelona’s next generation is an idea that will always appeal to the football romantic. Busquets still needs time to gain practical experience, develop his own methods and demonstrate his ability to manage players from the touchline. It is still early days, but it is refreshing to see Barça already thinking about the future and how life after Hansi Flick might look. While that scenario is unlikely to be anytime soon, the Catalan club are right to have a plan in place, and it remains to be seen how things pan out.

item.title: Mike Vrabel Gets Real on Drake Maye’s 2nd Quarter Interception
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Head coach Mike Vrabel of the New England Patriots looks on against the Chicago Bears during the first quarter of the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots runs off the field after being defeated by the Chicago Bears in the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty The New England Patriots fell to the Chicago Bears 30-24 on Thursday night, cutting the team’s three-game win-streak that had seen them otherwise unbeaten in October. In one of the key plays of the game late in the second quarter, quarterback Drake Maye threw a red-zone interception with 3:31 remaining on an intended end-zone pass to rookie tight end Eli Raridon. The Bears went on to score towards the end of the quarter, before a magical Rhamondre Stevenson effort as time was expiring in the second half bought the game back to within a score, 14-20. Drake Maye ‘Would Like That Throw to Eli Back’ – Mike Vrabel Speaking to the media after the game, head coach Mike Vrabel talked about Maye’s performance. And whilst he expressed positive sentiments about his star quarterback, he did note that the third-year QB would like to have the second-quarter interception back. "He gave us a chance" 🎙️ Mike Vrabel on Drake Maye's performance tonight against the Bears 👀 pic.twitter.com/1Yg3Sn8n3f — NESN (@NESN) October 23, 2026 “He gave us a chance, he competed. And I know he’d like to have that throw back to Eli, but I thought he really competed, and whether that was running around and scrambling or finding good places to go with the football.: Vrabel said postgame. “He gave us a chance, and I know he’d like to have that one back, and he’ll learn from it like he always does. I’m glad he’s ours.” Drake Maye Puts Up Strong Performance Despite Interception Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – OCTOBER 22: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots runs off the field after being defeated by the Chicago Bears in the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Although Vrabel; and likely Maye himself; was not thrilled with the play, Vrabel nonetheless expressed gratitude to have the elite young passer leading his team. The passer who consistently evaded swaths of pressure on Thursday night to make plays both inside and outside of the pocket, as Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen bought near-constant pressure off blitz packages. Even with the ugly interception, the young quarterback – and one of the elite signal callers in the game today – managed to put up a strong performance otherwise with 321 passing yards, a 77.4% completion percentage and 2 touchdowns and 1 pick. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Mike Vrabel Gets Real on Drake Maye’s 2nd Quarter Interception appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Whither Vladimir? (Part 2)
item.description: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 23: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. #27 of the Toronto Blue Jays watches the game in the seventh inning during game two of a double header against the Baltimore Orioles at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on September 23, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Tuesday, I looked at historical comps to Vladimir Guerrero jr.’s miserable 2026 season. The takeaway was that this kind of collapse is rare, occurring just about 1% of the time for players under 30 who don’t miss major time due to injury, that a lot of players who fall off a cliff like that never fully recover, but that Vlad’s youth, health, and the fact that the drop almost all came from power issues rather than walks or strikeouts means he has better than average odds of recovering. Today, I want to dig a little bit into what actually drove his 2026 fall off. The first thing to look at is whether there’s a significant shift in how he was pitched. The graph below shows the pitch types he’s seen by season in his career. The big thing to note is that over time he’s seeing somewhat fewer four-seamers and steadily more sinkers, with the two pitches almost equal in 2026. That makes sense, as Vlad’s weakness at the plate has always been the ability to elevate the ball. In his career, he has a -3 degree launch angle against sinkers compared to 14 degrees against four-seamers. He still hits sinkers very hard, but he struggles to elevate them enough to do damage. I don’t think pitch mix is a huge contributor to his 2026 struggles, though. For one, he has a .873 career OPS against sinkers, so while he’s not as good against them as four-seamers it isn’t as if they eat him up. For another, He hit the sinkers he saw this year pretty well (.849 OPS) but fell off against four seamers (.873, compared to .964 in his career). Vlad swings extremely hard, and that didn’t change this season. His 76.3mph average bat speed was in the 92nd percentile among qualified hitters, and while it was just slightly slower than 2025 it was significantly harder than 2023 or 2024. item.content:encoded: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 23: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. #27 of the Toronto Blue Jays watches the game in the seventh inning during game two of a double header against the Baltimore Orioles at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on September 23, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Tuesday, I looked at historical comps to Vladimir Guerrero jr.’s miserable 2026 season. The takeaway was that this kind of collapse is rare, occurring just about 1% of the time for players under 30 who don’t miss major time due to injury, that a lot of players who fall off a cliff like that never fully recover, but that Vlad’s youth, health, and the fact that the drop almost all came from power issues rather than walks or strikeouts means he has better than average odds of recovering. Today, I want to dig a little bit into what actually drove his 2026 fall off. The first thing to look at is whether there’s a significant shift in how he was pitched. The graph below shows the pitch types he’s seen by season in his career. The big thing to note is that over time he’s seeing somewhat fewer four-seamers and steadily more sinkers, with the two pitches almost equal in 2026. That makes sense, as Vlad’s weakness at the plate has always been the ability to elevate the ball. In his career, he has a -3 degree launch angle against sinkers compared to 14 degrees against four-seamers. He still hits sinkers very hard, but he struggles to elevate them enough to do damage. I don’t think pitch mix is a huge contributor to his 2026 struggles, though. For one, he has a .873 career OPS against sinkers, so while he’s not as good against them as four-seamers it isn’t as if they eat him up. For another, He hit the sinkers he saw this year pretty well (.849 OPS) but fell off against four seamers (.873, compared to .964 in his career). The shift also doesn’t look to be related to where pitchers attacked him. He actually saw more fastballs and off-speed pitches in the heart of the zone this season, compared to the last two: Instead, I think the issue lies with his timing. Vlad swings extremely hard, and that didn’t change this season. His 76.3mph average bat speed was in the 92nd percentile among qualified hitters, and while it was just slightly slower than 2025 it was significantly harder than 2023 or 2024. He has a relatively flat swing, with a 29 degree tilt that’s 3 degrees below mlb average. That number was up one degree from 2024 and 2025, but the difference isn’t substantial. His swing also didn’t get any longer. All in all, it doesn’t look like he changed his swing meaningfully this year. What did change was the type of contact he made. Vlad didn’t swing and miss more this season. In fact, his 82% contact rate was a career best and in the 73rd percentile in MLB, which is impressive for a player who swings as hard as he does. That contact wasn’t nearly as good, though. The panel below shows an assortment of swing metrics, comparing his 24-25 results to this year. His bat speed is about the same, with a few less average swings and slightly more extremely hard ones. His attack angle, which is the angle the barrel of the bat is traveling when it hits the ball, shows a significant shift, though. He hit a lot more balls on the downswing and fewer in positive territory, especially the 0-10 degree range. He is attack direction, which measures the horizonal direction of the barrel at contact, shows that he went up the middle and slightly the other way less often, and pulled the ball a bit more. Relatedly, his contact depth shifted forward, meaning he was meeting the ball out in front of the plate more often. All these signs point to him being a little in front of or behind the pitch more often, and meeting it at the ideal point less. The last plot shows the result. Squared-up fraction is the percentage of the maximum possible exit velocity (based on how fast the bat and ball are moving) that the batter achieves. Anything over 80% is considered squared up, meaning the batter got most of the possible impact on the ball. Vlad’s squared up fraction dropped in 2026, and the share of balls he really nailed, with 90% or better contact quality, fell dramatically. The result of all those changes can be seen in the heatmap below. The black shape represents roughly the combinations of launch angle and exit velocity that StatCast considers barrels, the type of batted ball that accounts for most extra base hits. The blue inside the barrel zone and the red areas just below and to the left of it show that a lot of barrels from previous seasons were either hit hard but too low, in the -10 to 10 degree area, or were at the right angle but just a little too soft. There’s also a fair bit of red above +40 degrees and below -20 degrees. Those are angles that basically never result in useful contact. It looks like he maid more really bad contact than in past seasons, in addition to less really good contact. My takeaway from all of this is that Vlad spent the whole season just a little off. His bat speed shows that he didn’t lose raw strength, and there’s nothing to suggest that his mechanics changed dramatically. He was just missing by a little bit, consistently. It’s surprising to have such a dramatic effect and not be able to isolate a dramatic cause, but there’s really no huge smoking gun here. It makes me wonder whether his vision really was an issue, or whether one of his nagging injuries was altering his swing just slightly, not in a way that shows up clearly in the metrics but enough to keep him from ever quite locking in. In terms of his prognosis, I think this has to be seen as good news. If he’d lost his eye, or his bat speed, or his ability to get the bat on the ball, we’d have reason to worry that his skills had eroded in a way that wasn’t going to come back. I don’t see evidence for that, though. On the other hand, there’s no obvious fix, either. There’s no obvious adjustment to undo, or tweak that will address a revealed weakness. He just has to get right. Whether the coaching staff can help him do that this winter is maybe the single most important question facing the Blue Jays’ long term future right now.

item.title: Harry Brook breaks Shubman Gill's fastest 200 record as Sri Lanka pull off historic ODI run chase
item.description: England captain Harry Brook made history by scoring the fastest double-century in One-Day International (ODI) cricket, but his record-breaking innings could not prevent Sri Lanka from securing a thrilling two-wicket victory in their tri-series match on Thursday. Sri Lanka chased down a target of 430 with one ball remaining, leaving England at the bottom of the standings after two defeats. Brook reached his double-century in just 114 balls, breaking the previous record of 117 deliveries held by India's Shubman Gill. The 27-year-old also became the first English batter to score an ODI double-century, surpassing Ben Stokes' previous national record of 182 runs. He smashed 202 runs off 116 balls, hitting 21 fours and 10 sixes before being caught by Sahan Arachchige off Janith Liyanage on the final ball of England's innings. Joe Root also contributed with 69 runs off 66 balls as England posted a massive 429-4. Brook, however, was disappointed that his historic achievement ended in defeat. "Unfortunately, it (the record) doesn't matter now. I thought we were going to be in a good position but, unfortunately, it doesn't even count," Brook said. "Heart-breaking. I think you've hit the nail on the head there. It's very disappointing that we haven't been able to defend 430, but that's life, that's cricket," he added. Sri Lanka pull off historic run chase Sri Lanka produced a remarkable batting display to complete the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history. Pavan Rathnayake led the charge with 130 off 106 balls, while Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both missed their centuries by just three runs. Sri Lanka needed six runs from the final two balls when Liyanage hit Josh Tongue for a six over long-off to seal victory with one delivery remaining. Tongue finished as England's leading wicket-taker with 3-79. Brook praised Sri Lanka's performance and admitted England failed to execute their bowling plans. "You don't see many teams chase down 430 and hats off to Sri Lanka. They've played exceptionally well. We couldn't execute our skills enough with the ball and, again, they've just played an absolute blinder there ..." England, who lost to Pakistan by 87 runs on Tuesday, now need to win their remaining two matches to keep their hopes of reaching the final in Lahore alive. "We'll have a good chat about it now and over the next couple of days. We've got a good opportunity in the next couple of games to really try and get to that final in Lahore."

item.title: Infantino re-election hopes boosted by Asia support
item.description: Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa (left) had previously criticised Gianni Infantino over the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme [Getty Images] Gianni Infantino's hopes of being re-elected Fifa president have been given a major boost by an endorsement from the head of the Asian Football Confederation. President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa Salman told the confederation's Congress in Tokyo - which was attended by Infantino - that "we reaffirm our full commitment, of course, to supporting you as you seek a new mandate as president". Sheikh Salman's support represents a significant u-turn just two months after he signed a joint letter with the heads of Uefa and Concacaf criticising Infantino over his failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. At the time the three confederations accused him of breaking trust "through deception" over the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme. But Sheikh Salman told the meeting in Japan it was time "to move forward". "I've spoken to a lot of members within this continent. I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well. Your support to Gianni is very clear," he added. "So that's why Gianni I want to make it clear: yes, we had some issues, we spoke about them in the past, but let's not relate the two things together. "The last few days we met in Zurich, you made it clear there was a clear understanding between us and that's why we're happy to have you here as well - we need to move forward. "As one Asian family, we are ready to move forward, united in your support, Gianni, I just want to make that clear." Alongside Infantino's power base in Africa and South America, Sheikh Salman's endorsement could be crucial in ensuring the Fifa president secures a fourth and final term. At the election in Rabat in March, Uefa will have 55 votes, Africa 54, Asia 46, Concacaf 35, Oceania 11 and Conmebol 10. The deadline for candidates to confirm they are standing against Infantino is 18 November - although none have yet filed and he could stand unopposed. At a meeting of Fifa's Council last week, Infantino apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan , but failed to offer a full explanation for how the proposal was devised. He also proposed to increase the amount of money handed out for football development across the world by $3.4bn (£2.6bn). Uefa has since told Fifa it must release key documents and answer all questions relating to its governance and decision-making by 2 November. Uefa gives Infantino two-week deadline to release key documents Could Wenger really take on Infantino and run for Fifa presidency?

item.title: How Thunder’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander losing 20-point streak earned extra admiration from Mark Daigneault
item.description: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images How Thunder’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander losing 20-point streak earned extra admiration from Mark Daigneault appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . OKLAHOMA CITY — With 1:43 left toward the end of a 96-84 win against the Denver Nuggets, Oklahoma City Thunder All-Star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander decided it was time to end his streak of scoring 20+ points in 141 consecutive regular-season games, head coach Mark Daigneault revealed. Amidst a cold shooting night, Gilgeous-Alexander found his offensive rhythm after halftime, scoring 13 of his 17 points in the second half against the Nuggets. The two-time MVP drained a dagger 3-pointer that extended the Thunder’s lead to 20 points (93-73), forcing Nuggets head coach David Adelman to empty his bench. That’s when Gilgeous-Alexander turned to Daigneault, and asked to be subbed out of the game. “It’s a historic record. So, it’s a bit of a dilemma if you’re in my position,” Daigneault said. “But he put me in a great position there. I would have left him. I was gonna leave him [in]. OKLAHOMA CITY — With 1:43 left toward the end of a 96-84 win against the Denver Nuggets, Oklahoma City Thunder All-Star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander decided it was time to end his streak of scoring 20+ points in 141 consecutive regular-season games, head coach Mark Daigneault revealed. Amidst a cold shooting night, Gilgeous-Alexander found his offensive rhythm after halftime, scoring 13 of his 17 points in the second half against the Nuggets. The two-time MVP drained a dagger 3-pointer that extended the Thunder’s lead to 20 points (93-73), forcing Nuggets head coach David Adelman to empty his bench. That’s when Gilgeous-Alexander turned to Daigneault, and asked to be subbed out of the game. “It’s a historic record. So, it’s a bit of a dilemma if you’re in my position,” Daigneault said. “But he put me in a great position there. I would have left him. I was gonna leave him [in]. Just another reason on the list of why I admire him.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It’s a historic record. So, it’s a bit of a dilemma if you’re in my position. But he put me in a great position there. I would have left him. I was gonna leave him (in). Daigneault commended Gilgeous-Alexander for making the call when he didn’t have to. “For the class that it shows and the perspective that it shows for him to say, “Hey, I’m out now, the game’s calling for me to be subbed out of the game,” that was his substitution, and of all the things that I admire about him, that’s toward the top of the list in terms of moments that I appreciate about him,” Daigneault said. “It shows tremendous class as a competitor.” For Gilgeous-Alexander, watching the Nuggets sub their starters out was all he needed to see to make the decision that his night was over, cementing a record that took over 60 years to break. “I was gonna go out there. Then, I saw that they had subbed. So, I thought, we should sub, too,” Gilgeous-Alexander said. “I feel like you always treat the game with respect. And God willing I have many more games to start another streak. So, it’s not that important.” Thunder All-Star Chet Holmgren admitted he’s not sure if he would have made the same choice if he were in Gilgeous-Alexander’s shoes, but commends SGA for making the admirable decision. “I asked him, I said, ‘You want to shoot some threes right here,’ and he’s like, “Nah,” then, he went up to Mark and subbed himself out,” Holmgren said. “I told him he’s a better man than me. I would have been shooting some pull-up threes. I think it was a selfless moment, and he’s a selfless guy. He’s one of the hardest workers that I know, and it shows up out there. And so does his leadership, and he does that the right way.” Gilgeous-Alexander was 6-for-19, including 3-for-11 from deep against the Nuggets. He also finished with three assists and one block. Jalen Williams’ 21 points led the Thunder, while Holmgren finished with 17 rebounds, 12 points, and four blocks. Oklahoma City improved to 2-0 on the regular season. item.title: Nick Woltemade makes history as he becomes only the third player to do this for Juventus
item.description: Nick Woltemade Juventus Goal Celebration Rennes Europa League Nick Woltemade has now made history with Juventus. The Newcastle United loan striker joining Darko Kovačević and Roberto Baggio. Juventus now with three players to score in each of their first three major European appearances. Nick Woltemade achieving this in the Europa League against NEC, Celta Vigo and now Rennes. Juventus went ahead through Zeki Çelik after five minutes, Nick Woltemade with the assist. Mousa Al-Taamari equalised and Boulaye Dia put Rennes ahead before half-time. Up stepped Nick Woltemade though to level with a very coolly taken second-half penalty under huge pressure in front of the Juve fans. The Newcastle United loan star was man of the match for Juventus and as well as his goal and assist, Big Nick linking up play so well as the Italian side created a host of chances. Very unlucky not to win the game as Jhon Lucumí’s late winner was ruled out for offside by VAR. Nick Woltemade spoke to Sky Sport Italia after the match: *“It’s definitely very bitter [not to win], given how much we produced in the second half,. We deserved to win. It didn’t happen and now we have to recover and think about Lecce. I politely asked Kolo Muani if I could take the penalty and he told me to go ahead. It went well and I scored. At the end I would have liked to get a third. The most important thing is to play a good game. Tonight we played with the right spirit and we’ll carry on like that.”* Great to see Nick Woltemade in such excellent European form, three goals and an assist from three Europa League starts. Also very refreshing to hear Big Nick having the confidence to want to take that high pressure penalty, wanting to take the responsibility. It has all been ridiculously over the top since his loan move (only last month!) as the Italian media have made the Newcastle United loan player a scapegoat for Juventus’ average start to the season, eighth in the table and only nine goals scored by Juve in seven league matches. This Nick Woltemade criticism (blindly parroted by the UK media) especially ludicrous considering Big Nick hasn’t yet had a chance to start a Serie A match, only 125 minutes in sub appearances. Big Nick the big target for blame and yet never having even started a league game yet, whilst as stated above, in all three Europa League matches when getting the chance to start he has scored, plus a vital assist as well last night. Following the game, Nick Woltemade made man of the match for Juventus with the highest rating of 8/10 from Goal going to the Newcastle United loan star: ‘The undisputed protagonist for Juventus. He provided the assist for Celik’s opener just six minutes in and remained the focal point of the attack throughout. item.title: Bears’ Cairo Santos sounds off on rebounding from miss to sink Patriots with 58-yard bomb
item.description: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Bears’ Cairo Santos sounds off on rebounding from miss to sink Patriots with 58-yard bomb appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson believes in Cairo Santos , and that is probably much easier to do because the longtime kicker strongly believes in himself. Following a potentially costly miss that could have swayed momentum in the New England Patriots’ favor, Santos quickly composed himself and fired a career-long 58-yard field goal that helped clinch a 30-24 win for his squad. While mental fortitude is mandatory for this position, the 34-year-old Brazilian displayed impressive tenacity by making a milestone kick just minutes after committing a blunder. “The misses annoy me, but like I can clear it so quick,” Santos said, per Adam Jahns of CHGO Sports. “Like when (it’s) the next opportunity, I just lock into my routine and I trust that I can execute.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Execute he did. The Tulane alum bounced the ball off the post on a 53-yard FG attempt with just over eight minutes left on the game clock. The miss enabled the Patriots to take over at their own 43-yard line and potentially capture the lead. Chicago’s defense held strong, however, and forced a three-and-out. A brutal Caleb Williams sack then gave the kicker another opportunity to leave his mark on this Week 7 Thursday Night Football matchup. Cairo Santos welcomed the chance for redemption, and for the first time in his 13-year NFL career, he connected on a 58-yarder. The Bears secured a 30-21 lead with 1:34 remaining, which meant the Patriots would need to complete a miraculous finish in order to snatch victory. They did not. Santos’ bomb proved to be the difference, and moreover, it showed just how resilient he can be when the pressure is approaching uncomfortable levels. The Bears (5-2) will vie for their third straight win when they face the Seattle Seahawks (3-3) in Week 8. Related: Bears’ Caleb Williams pours heart out to Cole Kmet after possibly serious knee injury Related: Patriots’ Christian Gonzalez can only tip his cap to Caleb Williams after loss to Bears

item.title: Arch Manning transfer rumors: LSU, Ole Miss, Oregon among top options if Texas QB leaves in 2027
item.description: Arch Manning transfer rumors: LSU, Ole Miss, Oregon among top options if Texas QB leaves in 2027 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . What was supposed to be Arch Manning's dream season at Texas has gone poorly. The Longhorns didn't even make it to the end of October before getting two losses, and Manning has not played well. Even Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian said after Texas' loss to Florida that he was going to give an uptick to Manning's backup, KJ Lacey. Although a benching of Manning appears unlikely, it is not entirely out of the realm of possibility. Thanks to how poorly his season has gone, there is speculation that he may forgo the 2027 NFL Draft and choose to stay in college for another season. While the expectation is that he will remain at Texas if he does stay, let's take a look at some of the best landing spots for Manning if he does decide to enter the transfer portal. MORE: Sporting News 2026 Midseason All-America college football team Arch Manning top transfer portal destinations LSU Tigers Manning played high school football for four seasons in Louisiana, playing out of Isidore Newman in New Orleans. His high school sits just 82 miles southeast of Baton Rouge, and Manning was born and grew up in Louisiana. If Manning wants to hone in on his development as a quarterback, LSU head coach Lane Kiffin has an impressive track record in doing so. He made Jaxson Dart into a first-round NFL Draft pick, and helped discover Trinidad Chambliss from DII Ferris State, who is expected to be a top signal-caller picked for 2027. Sam Leavitt hasn't played great so far this season, and although Kiffin won't admit it, he was the coach's fourth transfer choice behind Trinidad Chambliss, Brandon Sorsby and Washington's Demond Williams. What better way to start fresh for Manning than to return to his roots and play under an offensive mind like Kiffin? Georgia Bulldogs Georgia head coach Kirby Smart has historically stuck with quarterbacks he has recruited out of high school and developed in Athens. Speaking of, Smart and the Bulldogs were one of three finalists for Manning coming out of high school. But Smart has also landed some transfer portal quarterbacks as backups to Gunner Stockton, including Oregon transfer Bryson Beaver this year, and adding Jaden Rashada in 2024. Stockton is a fifth-year senior this season, and his backup, Ryan Puglisi has completed 36 passes for 413 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions his last two seasons. Getting a quarterback with real game experience like Manning might not be a bad idea for Smart, even if that's non-traditional for him. MORE: College football picks, predictions against the spread for Week 8 Ole Miss Rebels If Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding wants another way to beat Kiffin aside from his team's 32-24 victory earlier this season, look no further. Golding already successfully prevented Chambliss from leaving Ole Miss

What better way to start fresh for Manning than to return to his roots and play under an offensive mind like Kiffin? Georgia Bulldogs Georgia head coach Kirby Smart has historically stuck with quarterbacks he has recruited out of high school and developed in Athens. Speaking of, Smart and the Bulldogs were one of three finalists for Manning coming out of high school. But Smart has also landed some transfer portal quarterbacks as backups to Gunner Stockton, including Oregon transfer Bryson Beaver this year, and adding Jaden Rashada in 2024. Getting a quarterback with real game experience like Manning might not be a bad idea for Smart, even if that's non-traditional for him. MORE: College football picks, predictions against the spread for Week 8 Ole Miss Rebels If Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding wants another way to beat Kiffin aside from his team's 32-24 victory earlier this season, look no further. Golding already successfully prevented Chambliss from leaving Ole Miss and joining Kiffin at LSU. How about doing it a second time in a row by getting Manning to come to Oxford? Chambliss is going to the NFL after this season. It would also be incredibly cool to see Manning go where his grandfather, Archie, and uncle Eli played. That's not a bad recruiting pitch if you're Golding, either. In Oxford, Manning might have to compete for the starting job with current backup Deuce Knight, who transferred in from Auburn this offseason. But his game experience might give him an edge. Oregon Ducks Oregon head coach Dan Lanning has had an unexpectedly down year at quarterback this season. Starter Dante Moore is expected to miss a second consecutive game as he left the game against UCLA on Oct. 10 with a concussion. In his absence, he's shuffled between Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas, although neither of them have played all too great. Lanning has yet to name a starter between the two ahead of Oregon's game against Illinois this week, although Raiola appears to have an edge . Moore is expected to go to the NFL in 2027, and Raiola is a junior this season. The quarterback room is pretty wide open behind Raiola for next season. Although Oregon might be far from home for Manning, Lanning has a solid track record at transfer portal quarterbacks as Moore came in from UCLA, and Dillon Gabriel transferred in from Oklahoma in 2024. MORE: College Football Playoff bracket for Week 8 Indiana and Miami might make sense if Manning improves At this point, I think Indiana and Miami only really make sense for Manning on paper. While both teams have cashed in on landing some big-time transfer portal quarterbacks, such as Cam Ward and Carson Beck at Miami and Fernando Mendoza and Josh Hoover at Indiana. But I think for both schools to be interested in Manning, he will have to play a lot better than he has been. Beck and Hoover both had multiple seasons with over 3,000 yards passing, and had consistent success as a starter across multiple seasons. Mendoza had thrown for 4,712 with 30 touchdowns over two years with Cal. While Manning's stats are slightly similar, I don't think he's put enough good games on tape to where he'd be an attractive option for either school. Across his two seasons, he has 20 turnovers, and has not played well in his five losses to Ohio State, Florida and Georgia last season and vs. Oklahoma and Florida so far this year. Indiana and Miami will be likely to pursue a quarterback that's played much more consistent. But if Manning has a strong back half of the season, both schools could absolutely be in play. item.title: ‘That’s not who I am…’-Carmelo Anthony’s refusal sheds light on his NBA exit
item.description: Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images Carmelo Anthony has explained why he refused to embrace a bench role late in his NBA career, admitting he could not accept becoming a veteran mentor rather than a leading player. Accepting the supporting role can be tough for top stars, especially during the end of their careers. The former New York Knicks star believes accepting that position could change how people remember him, a mindset that may have contributed to the difficult end of his playing career. Anthony discussed the subject on his podcast, 7PM in Brooklyn , reflecting on the challenge of adjusting to a reduced role as a player’s abilities decline. Carmelo Anthony explains why he rejected a bench role Speaking on his podcast, Anthony made clear that he respected veterans who accepted supporting roles but did not see himself following the same path. He said: “I can’t take a Taj Gibson role, and I respect somebody like Taj Gibson to the utmost. But for me to take that role, no, that’s not who I am. I can’t accept that. I don’t want to accept that role.” Anthony also explained that he worried about how younger players would remember him if they only saw him as a bench player rather than the star he had been during his prime. “Once you’re seen in that light, that’s who you are. Even if it’s a kid who’s seeing you in that position, that’s the first thing that he’s going to see, which is the last thing of you. So now that’s the memory,” he added. His comments offer insight into the difficulties he faced towards the end of his career, particularly after his time with the Houston Rockets ended early amid questions about his attitude towards a reduced role. Anthony later found a place with the Portland Trail Blazers, where he returned to a starting role, before eventually accepting a bench position with the Los Angeles Lakers. However, opportunities became harder to find, and he ultimately left the NBA without securing the championship that had eluded him throughout his career. Well, that makes him one of the best ever to never touch the championship. The debate also highlights the challenge facing veteran stars as they age. LeBron James has shown a willingness to accept a smaller role in pursuit of team success, while Anthony’s comments suggest that protecting his identity as a star was a major consideration. Anthony remains involved in basketball through his work as a broadcaster and podcast host, giving him the opportunity to reflect on a career that brought both major success and a difficult final chapter. item.title: Bears’ Luther Burden III sends warning to defenses about tackling him: ‘It’s gonna be a problem’
item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Bears’ Luther Burden III sends warning to defenses about tackling him: ‘It’s gonna be a problem’ appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bears ended the three-game winning streak of the New England Patriots with a gutsy victory, 30-24, at Soldier Field on Thursday. The Bears improved to 5-2, while the Patriots fell to 4-3. Luther Burden III was instrumental in the tight win, scoring a big touchdown on four receptions for 130 yards. He found the end zone with 14 seconds left in the first half after catching Caleb Williams 24-yard pass. It gave the Bears extra momentum heading into the break, 20-7. They never relinquished the lead in the second half. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) After the game, the 22-year-old Burden explained why he is nicknamed “Problem Child.” “When I get the ball, it’s gonna be a problem. Especially with too much space. I might go the distance,” said the second-year wide receiver in the video posted by CHGO Bears. “When I get the ball it’s gonna be a problem ESPECIALLY with too much space.”😮‍💨 Luther Burden III on “Problem Child” nickname: pic.twitter.com/SeBvhJMMFo — CHGO Bears (@CHGO_Bears) October 23, 2026 Burden logged his first touchdown of the season. In seven games, he has 31 receptions on 48 targets for 361 yards. Fans loved the moniker for the two-time All-SEC First Team. “It fits my boy. ‘Problem Child’ it is,” said @DGoffsibley. “His swagger is literally the whole brand, and it works because he’s got the tape to back it up,” added @laura_piddle. “‘Problem Child,’ bro, really 😭😭😭😭,” wrote @HoodiLulu. “That’s my WR1,” stated @kingMeJayo. @EyeTestFF commented a GIF for good measure. pic.twitter.com/Qw8LQp7AMn — EyeTestFF (@EyeTestFF) October 23, 2026 Burden has never made a comment he did not like. In Week 5, he had a back-and-forth with Anthony Davis of the Washington Wizards on Instagram after the Bears were crushed by the Green Bay Packers. The Bears will visit the Seattle Seahawks in Week 8. item.title: 'No messing about' - Eddie Howe backed to replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United manager
item.description: Manchester United v Newcastle United - Carabao Cup Fourth Round - Getty Images Sport Former Bournemouth winger Marc Pugh has backed Eddie Howe to take over from under-fire head coach Michael Carrick at Manchester United. The 48-year-old tactician has emerged as a leading contender for the Old Trafford hotseat after Wednesday's humbling 4-1 Champions League defeat away at Como extended the club's winless run. Former winger endorses managerial contender Pugh believes his old boss possesses the ideal profile to revive the Red Devils should the hierarchy dismiss Carrick. Wednesday's loss in Italy stretched the club's winless streak to seven games across all competitions. According to talkSPORT , technical director Jason Wilcox favours appointing the 48-year-old if a change is made, though ex-Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann has also been sounded out . Relentless intensity suits struggling squad Sevilla v AFC Bournemouth - Pre-Season Friendly Signed by Howe in 2010, the 39-year-old former winger made 232 appearances under the Englishman during a nine-year stay at the Vitality Stadium that included promotions from both League One and the Championship. Speaking on talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Baker show on Thursday, Pugh insisted the demanding coach would immediately raise standards behind the scenes: "If I was Eddie, I'd jump at the chance, but to be honest, I think United need someone like Eddie. The intensity level in training will go up a notch. He won't stand for people sacking training off. "I'm not saying Michael does. I don't know what goes on behind the scenes at Old Trafford, at United, but he will make sure people that are playing on a Saturday and Tuesday, whenever it may be, that they are going to run and he plays high-press, high-intensity football. "There will be no messing about, that's for sure, but he's fantastic tactically, technically, he cares about his players and I think they can do a lot worse than Eddie, that's for sure." Silverware pedigree strengthens job credentials Howe has been out of work since departing Newcastle United in July following a successful five-year tenure at St James' Park. During his time on Tyneside, he twice secured Champions League qualification and lifted the 2025 Carabao Cup to end the Magpies' 70-year wait for major domestic silverware, building on two memorable spells at Bournemouth either side of a nine-month stint with Burnley. Having initially steered the Cherries out of League Two, he returned in 2012 to take them all the way to the Premier League. Asked whether his former manager would be tempted by the vacancy in Manchester, Pugh added: "I think jobs like that don't come around often and it's one of the best clubs in the world. You've got to jump at the chance in my eyes." Cherries clash tests dugout survival imago-sport-1084870206.jpg Despite the growing speculation surrounding his position, Carrick is set to remain in the dugout when United host Howe's former club Bournemouth on Sunday. item.title: How three men and one win can help Tottenham shake off ‘Spursy’ tag
item.description: How three men and one win can help Tottenham shake off ‘Spursy’ tag The mantra of being ‘Spursy’ has long been a source of irritation for Tottenham Hotspur fans – largely because it originates in a reality the club has been trying to shake. Relinquishing leads, wilting under pressure and a lack of collective belief has led to Spurs spending years trying to escape the label. Changing that reputation will take more than a new manager, a few impressive performances or promises of a brighter future. It requires a change in mentality — and there are hopes Roberto De Zerbi, alongside the grit of players such as Dejan Kulusevski and James Maddison, could help Spurs begin that process. De Zerbi has a clearly defined footballing philosophy, built around bravery in possession, intelligent movement and the willingness to take risks. His teams are expected to play with conviction rather than simply react to their opponents. It’s also painstakingly evident how much of passionate character he is and how unrelenting he is in relation to his methods. If De Zerbi can forge a sense of togetherness and belief in the current, supremely gifted playing squad, Tottenham are capable of creating a special time akin to the years under Mauricio Pochettino. However, the difference between a talented team and a successful one is often what happens when everything is going against it. Grit must become part of Tottenham’s identity Dejan Kulusevski and James Maddison’s importance to Tottenham cannot be understated and the duo offer an example of the character Tottenham need. Both bring personality and competitive edge, and neither is short of confidence when it comes to demanding the ball and trying to influence a game. Kulusevski’s directness and willingness to drive forward can give Spurs momentum when matches become scrappy. Maddison, meanwhile, has the technical quality and self-belief to take responsibility in possession rather than hide when the stakes rise. The midfield pair have also both returned from potential career-ending injuries and played a role in Spurs’ 3-1 win over Coventry on Monday night. Neither player can solve Tottenham’s mentality problem alone; that responsibility must be shared across the dressing room. But a team needs leaders who set standards in training, demand more from their teammates and refuse to accept a drop in intensity when a match becomes uncomfortable. That is where De Zerbi’s influence could prove important. A clear tactical identity can create confidence, while consistent expectations around work rate, concentration and accountability can help build trust between players. Team spirit is not simply about celebrating together after a win. It is about tracking back for a teammate, responding positively after conceding and remaining united when the crowd grows anxious. Relinquishing leads, wilting under pressure and a lack of collective belief has led to Spurs spending years trying to escape the label. Changing that reputation will take more than a new manager, a few impressive performances or promises of a brighter future. If De Zerbi can forge a sense of togetherness and belief in the current, supremely gifted playing squad, Tottenham are capable of creating a special time akin to the years under Mauricio Pochettino. However, the difference between a talented team and a successful one is often what happens when everything is going against it. Grit must become part of Tottenham’s identity Dejan Kulusevski and James Maddison’s importance to Tottenham cannot be understated and the duo offer an example of the character Tottenham need. Both bring personality and competitive edge, and neither is short of confidence when it comes to demanding the ball and trying to influence a game. Kulusevski’s directness and willingness to drive forward can give Spurs momentum when matches become scrappy. Maddison, meanwhile, has the technical quality and self-belief to take responsibility in possession rather than hide when the stakes rise. The midfield pair have also both returned from potential career-ending injuries and played a role in Spurs’ 3-1 win over Coventry on Monday night. Neither player can solve Tottenham’s mentality problem alone; that responsibility must be shared across the dressing room. But a team needs leaders who set standards in training, demand more from their teammates and refuse to accept a drop in intensity when a match becomes uncomfortable. That is where De Zerbi’s influence could prove important. A clear tactical identity can create confidence, while consistent expectations around work rate, concentration and accountability can help build trust between players. Team spirit is not simply about celebrating together after a win. It is about tracking back for a teammate, responding positively after conceding and remaining united when the crowd grows anxious. Stamford Bridge the ultimate test Tottenham have not had an unhappier away day destination in the Premier League era than Stamford Bridge. Spurs have only beaten Chelsea once there, in 2018, since the 1990s and face their London rivals this weekend. There have been embarrassing defeats, capitulations and the infamous Battle of the Bridge over recent years. With Tottenham recording their first win of the season against Coventry last time out, De Zerbi’s men will need to show huge character and collective resolve to get a result on Saturday. The returns of Maddison and Kulusevski increase the quality of the Spurs team but also shows the individual resilience of the players in question. The Spursy label will not disappear because of one good performance or result – but a spirited, competitive showing at Stamford Bridge would at least be the first step and show the fans the club is heading in the right direction.

item.title: Continuing To Improve The Cleveland Browns Heading Towards 2027 - Defensive Review
item.description: theOBR While I regularly write about next season and roster predictions, this looks more at what the team is likely to do. In this piece I want to focus on where the Browns need to improve to get to above average in each position room for 2027. It will focus much more on the starters rather than seeing anything in terms of depth. They have a fantastic amount of cash and draft picks at their disposal to keep adding more to this young talented roster. Edge Defender According to SūmerSports, the Cleveland Browns rank 11th in pressure rate and 7th in pressures generated as a defense this season. It is incredibly impressive when you consider they traded Myles Garrett and Alex Wright was injured. During the Andrew Berry era they have generally had a higher performing second edge, maybe Alex Wright can be that but it will depend how he bounces back from his injury. They will certainly be looking at drafting or adding more talent here in the offseason, their rotational depth is stacked, but they could do with a special player to lead the room, this will hopefully allow Verse to bounce back to his level with the Rams. Defensive Tackle The Browns have a stud with Graham but the question is what to do with Maliek Collins. He is playing really well the last five weeks but he will also turn 32 just before the draft, so it might be one where we need to see how he finished the season before making a decision. At the same time Adin Huntington has jumped forward too in the last few weeks after a poor start to the season. They could run it back, but at the same time I can see them adding one more and operating from a position of strength with Collins as a dominant third defensive tackle. Then moving on from Hall or Huntington at the end of training camp. Whatever they do they will be in a strong position next season. Linebacker The two starters are fantastic and will return next season. They need to find a more reliable third linebacker. Easton Mascarenas-Arnold's 36 career defensive snaps haven't convinced me that he can step in and start if there is an injury. Maybe he gets a chance to prove his point during this season. You don't need to spend much here, around $2-3m can get you an experienced third linebacker that can also play special teams. They aren't needed for defensive play in this scheme as it is two linebacker heavy, but it gives you injury protection. Cornerback Around 66% of snaps they will play a third cornerback in the slot. This issue with Myles Harden is the inconsistency. You have times when he is great and others when he is really struggling. Ideally they will want a better player here as well as more depth for injuries behind Ward and Campbell. Blackmon was serviceable but where most teams don't have three good cornerbacks, the chances of having real depth are incredibly thin. If they can draft someone the develop on the boundary and add more experience in the slot via free agency, it will put them in an even stronger spot next season. Safety

Then moving on from Hall or Huntington at the end of training camp. Whatever they do they will be in a strong position next season. Linebacker The two starters are fantastic and will return next season. They need to find a more reliable third linebacker. Easton Mascarenas-Arnold's 36 career defensive snaps haven't convinced me that he can step in and start if there is an injury. Maybe he gets a chance to prove his point during this season. You don't need to spend much here, around $2-3m can get you an experienced third linebacker that can also play special teams. They aren't needed for defensive play in this scheme as it is two linebacker heavy, but it gives you injury protection. Cornerback Around 66% of snaps they will play a third cornerback in the slot. This issue with Myles Harden is the inconsistency. You have times when he is great and others when he is really struggling. Ideally they will want a better player here as well as more depth for injuries behind Ward and Campbell. Blackmon was serviceable but where most teams don't have three good cornerbacks, the chances of having real depth are incredibly thin. If they can draft someone the develop on the boundary and add more experience in the slot via free agency, it will put them in an even stronger spot next season. Safety They will have a decision to make after the season of what to do with Hickman. Both Delpit and McNeil-Warren are here for the long term and will be starting next season. There has been a gentle increase in usage of a third safety with the team playing them 40-50% the last three weeks. This seems to be wider than just wanting to get McNeil-Warren on the field as it continued when Delpit went down and they brought Daniel Thomas in. This could open the door to keeping Hickman beyond this season, while Thomas played well, there is a benefit to having more depth. I can see them pushing to keep Hickman as long as he isn't wanting too much, especially if he is playing around 50% of snaps and providing quality depth at the same time. Special Teams I would expect the plan is to run it back. They could look to change their punter though if they are moving to being a top team. Corey Bojorquez's skill is flipping the field, if you are looking to punt and pin someone in deep, then there is probably someone else you can find. The fact they had three punters during camp and then one on the practice squad shows they want more. Coaching After a rough week one start, it feels like his work has been exceptional. Despite losing a superstar in Myles Garrett they have spread the burden across the rest of the roster and everyone is stepping up. We will need to see it over a larger period but this feels like a very talented defensive coaching staff. Don't be shocked if defensive coordinators are hired from this group over the next few years. Conclusion The shopping list is very low, there are no desperate needs, more areas it would be nice to upgrade, such as: Starting Edge Defensive Tackle Help (If Collins Slows) Third Linebacker Slot Cornerback Cornerback Depth Hickman Re-signed Punter Upgrade It feels like the Browns are approaching an offseason where it is a quarterback and luxury picks/additions. It is important that they don't go and waste that advantage. The Chiefs should have taken Tee Higgins in the 2020 draft to add more weapons but thought a running back would help them more and selected Clyde Edwards-Helaire. Their struggle with pass catchers continues to this day where as they have found alternative backs fairly easily. While people regularly talk about 'best player available' the Browns could operate from that position in the 2027 draft. It is why coming into this season I was incredibly high on the Browns in 2027 and I see no reason to pause the optimism.

item.title: Roma consider Alejandro Balde to add squad depth
item.description: Roma consider Alejandro Balde to add squad depth In January, Tony D’Amico will be tasked with satisfying the demands of Gian Piero Gasperini, who has publicly stated that his squad is short. Roma’s sporting director agrees with the coach, which is why he’s already working to best plan the next transfer window. He has two objectives: a striker and a central midfielder. In addition to Oosterwolde, the new name is Barcelona’s Balde. The 2003-born player has already played 170 games for the Spanish club, but this season he’s not finding much playing time under Hans-Dieter Flick. The left-back is finding little playing time at Barcelona, ​​which is why he could leave in January. As reported by Il Messaggero, given his limited playing time with Flick, Mendes, the 2003-born player’s agent (the same as Rodrigo Mora), has offered him to the Giallorossi. It remains to be seen what developments will take place in the coming weeks.
