item.title: Browns’ Jared Verse can’t believe a teammate was doing ‘calculus’ before a game
item.description: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images Browns’ Jared Verse can’t believe a teammate was doing ‘calculus’ before a game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Cleveland Browns defensive end Jared Verse has revealed an unusual story about his teammate Carson Schwesinger, whose preparation for a preseason game apparently included solving an advanced mathematics problem. Verse recently praised Schwesinger’s reliability and football instincts, but his latest revelation highlights another surprising side of the linebacker’s personality. According to Andrew Siciliano, Verse said Schwesinger was “doing advanced calculus on his laptop” during the Browns’ flight to a preseason game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The revelation offers a glimpse into how differently NFL players spend their time before taking the field. WHile some athletes use team flights to review film, listen to music, relax, Schwesinger apparently had a more academic activity on his schedule. As a linebacker, Schwesinger is responsible for reading offensive formations, reacting quickly to developing plays and making critical defensive decisions. His apparent interest in advanced mathematics adds another dimension to his reputation as one of Cleveland’s dependable defensive players. The story also follows Verse’s glowing assessment of Schwesinger after the Browns defeated Baltimore Ravens 13-10. Schwesinger recorded 13 tackles and forced a crucial fumble in that victory, further strengthening his standing within Cleveland’s defense. His performance was especially noteworthy after he dealt with an ankle injury ahead of the Ravens matchup. For Verse, the calculus anecdote provides another reason to appreciate his teammate’s unusual conbination of interests and abilities. Whether studying complicated equations or diagnosing an opposing defense, Schwesinger appears comfortable taking on demanding challenges. The unexpected detail adds a lighter perspective to Cleveland’s locker room, showing how players can balance their professional football responsibilities with interests beyond the sport. item.title: Can Jeremy Doku hit the heights of Vinicius Jr & Luis Diaz? Man City star told where he needs to improve in order to join the global elite of left wingers
item.description: Jeremy Doku Luis Diaz Vinicius Junior 2026-27 - Getty/GOAL Doku joined City in a £55m transfer Doku’s game is all about running at opposition full-backs and forcing them onto the back foot. His pace allows direct bursts into the final third to be made, while his technical ability means that defenders can be left tied up in knots . Those qualities were first showcased when making a senior breakthrough in his homeland with Anderlecht. It was never going to take long for such potential to be noted, with Rennes being the ones to take him to France in 2020. Three seasons there saw his output in the goal contributions department continue to rise, with leading sides from across Europe paying close attention to a talented playmaker with a low centre of gravity. City ultimately won the race for a much sought-after signature, with the Premier League heavyweights parting with a £55 million ($74m) transfer fee. Doku had to prove his worth to demanding Catalan coach Pep Guardiola. He was not always a guaranteed starter during the early part of his time in England, but a more regular role was eventually nailed down . Premier League, FA Cup, Carabao Cup, Community Shield and FIFA Club World Cup triumphs have been savoured with the Blues. Can Doku emulate output of Vini Jr & Diaz? Can Doku emulate output of Vini Jr & Diaz? There is the promise of even more to come from Doku, with the general consensus being that he can become more prolific on the goal front - having never previously broken into double figures across a single campaign. His pace allows direct bursts into the final third to be made, while his technical ability means that defenders can be left tied up in knots . Those qualities were first showcased when making a senior breakthrough in his homeland with Anderlecht. It was never going to take long for such potential to be noted, with Rennes being the ones to take him to France in 2020. Three seasons there saw his output in the goal contributions department continue to rise, with leading sides from across Europe paying close attention to a talented playmaker with a low centre of gravity. City ultimately won the race for a much sought-after signature, with the Premier League heavyweights parting with a £55 million ($74m) transfer fee. Doku had to prove his worth to demanding Catalan coach Pep Guardiola. He was not always a guaranteed starter during the early part of his time in England, but a more regular role was eventually nailed down . Premier League, FA Cup, Carabao Cup, Community Shield and FIFA Club World Cup triumphs have been savoured with the Blues. Can Doku emulate output of Vini Jr & Diaz? Since then, one or two players came into the national team and Jeremy will have some difficulties to get back in the starting XI with Belgium. “But if he plays with Man City and is in good shape, he will always be on the team sheet.” Belgian believes he can be one of the best Doku believes that he can become one of the best around, telling The Guardian in April of his efforts to emulate Vini and Co: “I feel like if I have goals we are talking about a different conversation. Assists - I’m fine. “I have to be more in the areas where you can score easy goals, tap-ins. When I look at my goals, every time they are with dribbles. I want to score even five tap-ins a-season – that would make a big difference. “A winger needs to score. If I have those goals then I believe that I can get there to be the world’s best winger, for sure, 100%.” FFP saga seeing transfer talk generated FFP saga seeing transfer talk generated Doku’s ambition is to be admired , and every player should always be striving for continuous improvement. The odd distraction has, however, crept in at City - with 114 Financial Fair Player (FFP) charges and the threat of serious punishments hanging over the Etihad Stadium . It has been suggested that City could be stung with a points deduction that leads to them being relegated into the Championship. Doku will not want to be playing second tier football at this stage of his career, with potential transfer destinations for 2027 already being speculated on.

item.title: Zach Ertz shares message for Commanders WR Terry McLaurin
item.description: The 2025 season was a difficult one for the Washington Commanders . After coming off a 12-win season and the franchise’s first appearance in the NFC Championship Game in 33 years, the Commanders were crushed by injuries. Quarterback Jayden Daniels missed 10 games, wide receiver Terry McLaurin missed seven and tight end Zach Ertz suffered a devastating knee injury in Week 14. Daniels and McLaurin returned in 2026, while Ertz last played in the burgundy and gold last December against the Vikings. Not wanting to end his career on that note, Ertz, 36, rehabbed and returned to the Philadelphia Eagles in September, where he spent the first 8.5 seasons of his NFL career. Ertz spent the past two seasons with Washington, where he was one of Daniels’ top two targets, alongside McLaurin. Ertz stayed close with his former Commanders teammates. When McLaurin suffered his own devastating knee injury in Monday’s loss to the San Francisco 49ers, Ertz took to Instagram to show him some love. Ertz and McLaurin were both leaders for the Commanders during their time together. While Ertz may have moved on to a division rival, he enjoyed his time in Washington, playing with guys like Daniels and McLaurin. McLaurin was diagnosed with a torn patellar tendon in his left knee. It’s a devastating injury, especially for a wide receiver who will turn 32 next season. While McLaurin is under contract with the Commanders next season, there’s no more guaranteed money remaining, meaning they could move on from him with no penalty. This article originally appeared on Commanders Wire: Zach Ertz shares message for Commanders WR Terry McLaurin

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: A Q&A on the state of NIL: College agents open up about negotiations, transfer decisions, more
item.description: A Q&A on the state of NIL: College agents open up about negotiations, transfer decisions, more originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The modern era of college football recruiting is -- in some ways -- the wild west. Thanks to NIL, revenue sharing and players being able to enter the transfer portal, it has become one of the most chaotic parts of the sport. One of the people tasked with helping players navigate it all are name, image and likeness agents. In addition to a wide variety of other responsibility, agents help players broker NIL deals, choose which school is best for them and help them maximize their market value. The Sporting News spoke with a couple of NIL agents in Charles Cox of Red Envelope Sports and Peter Webb of QB Reps to learn more about how the industry works and about what being an NIL agent means. Red Envelope represents several NFL, college and high school athletes, including New Orleans Saints receiver Devaughn Vele and Washington State quarterback Caden Pinnick. QB Reps, which only signs quarterbacks, features clients in USC's Jayden Maiava, Wake Forest's Gio Lopez, Vanderbilt's Jared Curtis and Tennessee's George MacIntyre as well as Los Angeles Rams rookie Ty Simpson and Denver's Bo Nix in the NFL. Below, both Cox and Webb discuss a number of topics, from who they negotiate with at the schools to how transfer decisions are made. MORE: Here are college football's 30 highest paid players TSN: How long have you been in the business and how did you get involved in the business? He represents three NFL head coaches [Jim Harbaugh, Sean Payton and Mike McCarthy]. Don had heard I had sold my company and he had rebranded his NFL agency to Red Envelope Sports about five years ago, and wanted someone to take it over. Long story short, [I] ended up buying the agency from him. I took over the NFL agency. We started the NIL division about two years ago. [We] just tried to approach it in the same way we approached our NFL side of the business in a boutique-like way, offering families senior agent experience." item.content:encoded: A Q&A on the state of NIL: College agents open up about negotiations, transfer decisions, more originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The modern era of college football recruiting is -- in some ways -- the wild west. Thanks to NIL, revenue sharing and players being able to enter the transfer portal, it has become one of the most chaotic parts of the sport. One of the people tasked with helping players navigate it all are name, image and likeness agents. In addition to a wide variety of other responsibility, agents help players broker NIL deals, choose which school is best for them and help them maximize their market value. The Sporting News spoke with a couple of NIL agents in Charles Cox of Red Envelope Sports and Peter Webb of QB Reps to learn more about how the industry works and about what being an NIL agent means. Red Envelope represents several NFL, college and high school athletes, including New Orleans Saints receiver Devaughn Vele and Washington State quarterback Caden Pinnick. QB Reps, which only signs quarterbacks, features clients in USC's Jayden Maiava, Wake Forest's Gio Lopez, Vanderbilt's Jared Curtis and Tennessee's George MacIntyre as well as Los Angeles Rams rookie Ty Simpson and Denver's Bo Nix in the NFL. Below, both Cox and Webb discuss a number of topics, from who they negotiate with at the schools to how transfer decisions are made. MORE: Here are college football's 30 highest paid players TSN: How long have you been in the business and how did you get involved in the business? Charles Cox: "A longtime friend Don Yee, he's represented Tom Brady since Tom came out of Michigan, still represents Tom. He represents three NFL head coaches [Jim Harbaugh, Sean Payton and Mike McCarthy]. Don had heard I had sold my company and he had rebranded his NFL agency to Red Envelope Sports about five years ago, and wanted someone to take it over. Long story short, [I] ended up buying the agency from him. I took over the NFL agency. We started the NIL division about two years ago. [We] just tried to approach it in the same way we approached our NFL side of the business in a boutique-like way, offering families senior agent experience." Peter Webb: "I've been a sports agent for 22 years. I've never done anything else in my career since graduating law school, and worked with professional athletes in a lot of different sports. I always recruited at the college level and represented them as professional athletes. Five years ago, instead of recruiting them when they're sophomores or juniors in college, we started recruiting when they were in high school. So it's not like my job changed, to be honest. We just started recruiting them earlier." TSN: What does the process of finding a player a fit and matching that with compensation work? Webb: " When a kid is trying to pick a school, we're talking to Michigan, we're talking to Notre Dame, we're talking to Florida. We're helping them understand what that all looks like. Not just necessarily their financial package, because we really try to stay away from that. We're concentrating on the school, the location, their community, their track record, their coaching staff, the quarterbacks that have come through that, their process, like their recruiting class, the development, like we're looking at a lot, a lot of different things. The financial package for us, we try to make that come in after they've already selected the school they're going to." Cox: "We try to focus on generating the best football outcome for the player, and if you do that, the money is highly correlated with that if you go find the best spot. In this day and age, you try to focus on head coach security, right? Because you don't want to put a young man into a program where he could have to be there for six or 12 months and have to leave immediately. Which is hard, right? Because the coaches leave just as much as the players." Webb: "Every year when we are dealing with the top programs in the country, I already can tell a kid 'hey, if your final five are LSU, Bama, Tennessee, Georgia, and Miami, I already have a really good idea what it's going to look like for all these schools, they're all going to be competitive. So just go pick the best school for you, and then I'll make it work.'" Cox: "Obviously, the player has to build a great relationship with the position coach because that's who they're going to spend the vast majority of their time with, right? So all those things when you huddle up with a family and and try to figure out." MORE: How Michigan's Bryce Underwood is failing to live up to massive NIL deal TSN: Who are you typically communicating with at schools? Is it general managers, coaches or both? Cox: "When you're dealing with NIL, FBS, Power-Four schools, the Group of Six schools, virtually everyone has a general manager. And if it's not a general manager on paper, it's kind of a de facto GM." Webb: " I'm talking to the head coaches. I'm talking to offensive coordinators, and I'm talking to the quarterback coaches as well as their GM and recruiting coordinator, director of player personnel." Cox: "I never call coaches, that isn't my thing. I think they're a little bit out of the loop on the money. That's got to be frustrating for them, that they're kind of taken out of the money piece. I don't know if they don't like dealing with agents or they're kind of just annoyed by the dynamic of them being left out of such an important piece of the puzzle." TSN: December is a chaotic time, as the Early Signing Period coincides with the coaching carousel and the College Football Playoff. What is it like navigating that? Cox: " I've got a very transactional background, so it's not crazy to me. It's a blast. Solving problems with a gun to your head, that's fun to me. It's going to be crazy for the coaches and the staff because they aren't classically trained in this. These guys are classically trained in other things. They have God-given abilities to communicate and train these kids and inspire them on the field that they're not good at this stuff, right? That doesn't make them bad coaches or bad professionals, they're being asked to do things they have no track record in. This is human resources." Webb: "A lot goes into the portal because sometimes kids don't want to transfer, but they get recruited from other schools and other coaches. 'hey, come here, making promises—come here, you'll play right away. We can get you on the field. Using that angle of playing time can be very attractive. That's that's one. The second part is sometimes you have boosters and donors and collectives, calling and offering extremely, you know, lucrative financial package to come somewhere else and play." Cox: " How the portal is structured with now 10 days in the first week of January, much of [that] crosses over with some of the FBS schools starting school. It's ridiculous that the concept of GMS and agents speaking is somehow looked down upon by the industry. It'd be ridiculous to ask these young men to go find a new place, negotiate their deal, and fly around on official visits in 10 days, yeah, and then enroll in a new school without professional help." MORE: Who are college football's highest paid head coaches? TSN: What are conversations like for players wanting to enter the transfer portal or stay put? Cox: " We play that role of insurance agent. That if things go bad at the last minute, when a school tells you, 'Hey, I think you should find a new place to play—which they do, by the way—right at the end of the semester, or something changes at the last minute in November, before signing day. We can go create opportunities out of thin air because we're always in the mix with all these FBS schools." Webb: "Our job is really to say 'look, if you take the money out of it, what is the best scenario for you to develop and get on the field?' Because if your dream

item.title: New Zealand vs. India prediction, team news, pitch report and betting tips for 2nd T20I
item.description: New Zealand have two days to fix a problem that 225 runs could not hide. They host India in the second T20I at Hagley Oval on Saturday, trailing 1-0 in the five-match series after a four-wicket defeat. Glenn Phillips struck 82 not out from 40 balls and Finn Allen added 45 from 24, yet Sanju Samson's 67 from 33 and a 93-run opening stand with Abhishek Sharma put the chase in India's hands. Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell dragged the contest back in the middle overs, but Shreyas Iyer's 42 and Naman Dhi's unbeaten 42 from 15 balls finished it with two balls to spare. The hosts must now find a way through India's top order, and they will have to do it against a side that won without the rested Jasprit Bumrah. MORE: Virat Kohli vs Babar Azam: Who is the greatest? New Zealand vs. India 1st T20I prediction: Who will win? New Zealand have the better case to level the series at Hagley Oval on Saturday. They scored 225 for 4 and lost by two balls, with Allen dropping a sitter at long-on that let Iyer off on 27. Their new-ball bowlers conceded 48 in two overs and sent down four wides in the first five, and those errors are correctable. India, meanwhile, are still adjusting after a long flight, and their bowling looked thin. Bhuvneshwar Kumar went for 49 and Axar Patel for 51, and New Zealand hit 67 off the last 30 balls. Glenn Phillips and Allen will fancy another big total on a ground they now know well. TSN Prediction: New Zealand to win. item.title: Where to watch Kentucky vs. Texas Tech basketball: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for exhibition game
item.description: Where to watch Kentucky vs. Texas Tech basketball: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for exhibition game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . A Top 25 preseason clash is on tap Friday as No. 23 Kentucky hosts No. 19 Texas Tech in Lexington. It's the lone exhibition game for the Red Raiders, but it will be a good chance for Grant McCasland to see what he has against quality competition. The key storyline for Texas Tech after making the NCAA tournament five of the last six years is the status of JT Toppin, who tore his ACL in mid-February. His rehab process is ongoing and it sounds like he won't rejoin the Red Raiders until around the start of conference play. Kentucky has three preseason games on its slate, and this one should provide the best measuring stick on the heels of a 20-point win over Little Rock last week. Transfers Milan Momcilovic (16 points, seven rebounds), Alex Wilkins (11 points) and Zoom Diallo (seven points, five assists, five rebounds) got their feet wet in that one and more reps can only help them work into Mark Pope's system. It should be a good one at Rupp Arena. Here's all you need to know to tune in. Where to watch Kentucky vs. Texas Tech basketball TV channel: None Live stream: SEC Network+ via ESPN app Friday's Kentucky vs. Texas Tech exhibition game will not air on a traditional TV channel but can be streamed live on SEC Network+ via the ESPN app . Now you can watch ESPN without cable. item.content:encoded: Texas' make-or-break moment arrives for Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Texas coach Steve Sarkisian used the "rearview mirror-windshield" analogy at his press conference Tuesday to describe the last two weeks. It's about what lies ahead for No. 19 Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) against No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1 SEC). The Longhorns and Rebels meet at 7:30 p.m. ET in the "Saturday Night Football" spotlight game on ABC at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. The rear view shows back-to-back losses to Oklahoma and Florida that have dropped Texas from No. 1 in the AP Poll — 18 spots in two weeks. The Rebels are in front now, and a loss here would be much harder to leave behind for Sarkisian, quarterback Arch Manning, edge rusher Colin Simmons and the Longhorns as a whole. "The key to the drill for us moving forward is we have to have constructive conversations," Sarkisian said at a press conference Monday . "We've had those. It's easy to listen to the outside noise and the sky is falling and the season is over. What are we going to do next year? Hey, man we're 4-2. Let's be part of the solution. Let's go 1-0 this week and let's get to 5-2." What if that doesn't happen? Welcome to the make-or-break moment for the Longhorns in 2026 and the potential fallout if Texas suffers that third loss. MORE: Sporting News Midseason All-America team 'Arch can play better': Will Texas QB answer? Sarkisian stirred up a quarterback controversy of sorts – even if he confirmed Manning remains the starter for the Week 8 matchup against Ole Miss. Sarkisian confirmed quarterback KJ Lacey will get first-team reps in practice . Will that be any different than previous weeks? "Not to me but we'll see how the week goes," Sarkisian said. This is a moment for Manning, however. The redshirt junior quarterback remains the most-talked about QB in college football the last two seasons. To be clear, there was no way Manning would meet the hype and expectations heaped on the nephew of NFL legends Peyton and Eli Manning — the latter who starred with the Rebels from 1999-2003. "Arch can play better for us," Sarkisian said. "He's our starter, but I need to see a better version of Arch Manning like I need to see a better version of a lot of guys on our offensive football team right now." Manning agreed. "I haven't put good film on tape the past five weeks," Manning said . "I'm going to be better. I'm going to better for myself, I'm going to better my teammates and I'm going to better for my coaches. What is wrong with Arch? Defenses are taking the deep ball away, which is the strength in Manning's game. Manning had 13 TDs and three interceptions on passes of 20 yards or more last season, according to PFF.com . This year, he has two TDs and three interceptions. In the last two weeks, Manning is 3 of 8 for 145 yards with one TD and one interception on passes of 20 yards or more. Manning also is 17 of 29 (58.6%) for 181 yards one TD and one interception when not being blitzed – an average of 6.2 yards per attempt that has knocked the explosives out of the passing attack. So, what is the solution? "I feel like I'm being too hesitant to be honest, I'm going to die on the hill of I'm letting it rip," Manning said. How important is this start? Win, and all that noise dies down like it did after the 24-23 victory against No. 1 Ohio State on Sept. 12 . Struggle and lose, and the rep count for Lacey will be a talking point and the rumors of Manning either entering the transfer portal or the 2027 NFL Draft will continue to swell. How has Manning responded after a meeting with Sarkisian this week? "He has a chip on his shoulder and I appreciated it," Sarkisian said. MORE: How far is Arch Manning's 2027 NFL Draft stock falling? Can Steve Sarkisian turn two-loss Texas around? Sarkisian pointed to the reasons for the shocking 27-24 loss to Florida in Week 7. The Longhorns had just 19 total offensive plays in the second half. Sarkisian lamented a “crummy call” on a rollout pass with Manning and pointed to the parity in the SEC. After all, Florida beat Ole Miss 52-28 on Sept. 26. "The biggest area where I was disappointed — and I think we all were and all are — we just were really poor in critical situations in the game," Sarkisian said. That tends to fall on coaching. Sarkisian does deserve credit for back-to-back College Football Playoff appearances in 2023-24. Texas has a 39-10 record since 2023 – the sixth-best record among Power 4 schools behind Ohio State (43-7), Georgia (42-7), Oregon (42-7), Notre Dame (40-8) and Ole Miss (39-8). The Longhorns are tied with the Buckeyes and Bulldogs for most NFL Draft picks the last three years at 29. But this year was supposed to be different. The Athletic reported Texas spends between $45-55 million on NIL — and Manning, edge rusher Colin Simmons, tackle Trevor Goosby and receiver Cam Coleman are expected to be first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft . A third loss would make the College Football Playoff a long-shot for the third straight season, and Sarkisian would take heat for under-performing with a loaded roster. Would it be time to hand someone else the keys to the Lamborghini ? The hot-seat talk would heat up exponentially for Sarkisian, and the question at hand is simple. Sarkisian had back-to-back five-star quarterbacks in Quinn Ewers and Manning. The Longhorns have played for a SEC championship and reached the College Football Playoff semifinals in that stretch. But Texas is 7-9 against top-10 teams and 3-7 against top-five teams under Sarkisian. MORE: A college football midseason report card Will Texas drama continue? As if that’s not enough, Simmons — a Sporting News Midseason All-American who leads the FBS with 10.5 sacks — is expected to miss a few weeks with a high ankle sprain . This is the latest setback for the Longhorns, who have had drama attached to most of their games this season. In Week 2, it was the fallout from the postgame interview with Holly Rowe. Simmons was penalized for “simulating using the restroom” during a 20-17 victory against Tennessee on Sept. 26, and the fallout from the back-to-back losses to Oklahoma and Florida still stands. "You deal with things every year," Sarkisian said. "Some are more public than others, but you deal with stuff every year but you manage them accordingly as they come." Now, the soap-opera season continues against the Rebels, and a trip to No. 18 LSU is still on the schedule for Nov. 18. Can Texas silence the noise in prime time?

item.title: Rival watch: Jose Mourinho’s El Clasico plan reveals how Real Madrid intend to face Barcelona
item.description: Rival watch: Jose Mourinho’s El Clasico plan reveals how Real Madrid intend to face Barcelona Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho is preparing to make several tactical decisions for Sunday’s El Clasico against Barcelona. Los Blancos come into this game hoping to close the six-point gap that Hansi Flick’s Barça have established at the top of the table. According to MARCA , Federico Valverde, Arda Guler and Yan Diomande are expected to occupy important roles in Madrid’s starting XI. Mourinho’s plan involves deploying Valverde at right-back, Guler on the right wing and Diomande on the left, while Aurelien Tchouameni and Eduardo Camavinga form a double pivot in midfield. Mourinho plans a different midfield and attacking structure Valverde’s expected inclusion at right-back would continue a tactical adjustment that has recently helped Madrid improve their possession game. The Uruguayan offers energy, defensive recovery and the ability to move into midfield when Madrid build attacks. Arda Guler is expected to start on the right wing against Barcelona. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Ahead of him, Guler would provide creativity from the right flank, using his left foot to drift inside and connect with Madrid’s central players. Meanwhile, Tchouameni and Camavinga would give Mourinho a physically strong midfield partnership capable of protecting the defence and competing for second balls. Diomande’s proposed role on the opposite wing would add pace and directness, and he will look to target Xavi Espart, who is likely to start at right-back for Barça . What Mourinho’s plan means for Barcelona For Hansi Flick, the reported set-up offers several tactical clues ahead of Sunday’s encounter. Guler’s tendency to move inside could create combinations with Valverde, making Barcelona’s left-sided defensive organisation particularly important. However, that movement could also leave space behind Valverde when Madrid commit players forward. Barcelona’s attackers must be prepared to exploit those situations quickly rather than allowing Madrid to recover their defensive shape. Tchouameni and Camavinga could start together in midfield for El Clasico. (Photo by Giuseppe CACACE / AFP) (Photo by GIUSEPPE CACACE/AFP via Getty Images) The Tchouameni-Camavinga partnership presents another challenge. Their physicality could make central progression difficult. Barça ‘s midfield is the best there is in world football, and they will have to use their technical prowess to beat Madrid’s physicality. Madrid have looked better in these last two games since Jose Mourinho made these tactical adjustments, and Barça need to be wary of those changes. However, playing at the Camp Nou , Flick’s side should determine how the game is played, and it remains to be seen how Barça set up against Madrid.

item.title: Here's when Mercedes could win their ninth F1 Constructors' title
item.description: Mercedes are moving closer to securing their ninth Formula 1 Constructors' Championship, having established a commanding advantage over their rivals throughout the 2026 season. With the campaign entering its final six rounds, the Silver Arrows are now approaching the point at which they could mathematically seal the title, but several scenarios remain possible. The German manufacturer currently leads the standings with 578 points, ahead of Ferrari on 444, McLaren on 339 and Red Bull on 332. Mercedes have claimed 11 victories in the opening 17 Grands Prix, with Kimi Antonelli and George Russell occupying the top two positions in the Drivers' Championship. A ninth Constructors' Championship would be Mercedes' first since 2021, when the team secured its eighth consecutive title. However, the championship cannot be decided at this weekend's United States Grand Prix, regardless of the results in Austin. What does Mercedes need to secure the championship? With six races remaining and no further Sprint events scheduled, a maximum of 258 points is still available in the Constructors' Championship. Each team can collect up to 43 points per Grand Prix by finishing first and second. Even if Antonelli and Russell secure a one-two finish in Austin while both Ferrari drivers fail to score, Mercedes' advantage would only increase to 177 points. That would not be enough to settle the championship, as 215 points would remain available over the final five rounds. Mexico City, on 1 November, therefore represents the first mathematical opportunity for Mercedes to claim the title. Following that race, only 172 points will remain available, meaning the Silver Arrows must leave Mexico with an advantage that Ferrari cannot overturn. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures For Mercedes to achieve that, they would need to extend their current lead by at least 38 points across the United States and Mexican Grands Prix. Even in the most favourable scenario in Austin, with Mercedes scoring 43 points and Ferrari none, the Italian team would still need to be prevented from recovering the deficit in Mexico. Mercedes have outscored Ferrari by an average of 7.6 points per Grand Prix this season. If that trend continues, the championship could instead be decided at the São Paulo Grand Prix on 8 November, when just 129 points would remain available. Antonelli could become world champion before Mercedes While Mercedes must wait until at least Mexico to secure the Constructors' Championship, Antonelli could wrap up the Drivers' title at this weekend's United States Grand Prix. The Italian currently leads team-mate Russell by 102 points, with Lewis Hamilton a further nine points behind. item.title: Video: Khamzat Restrained During RAF Brawl — ‘I’ll F—k You Up Bro!‘
item.description: NEWARK, NEW JERSEY - MAY 09: Khamzat Chimaev of Russia prepares to face Sean Strickland in the UFC middleweight championship fight during the UFC 328 event at Prudential Center on May 09, 2026 in Newark, New Jersey. (Photo by Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC) Real American Freestyle (RAF) is ostensibly a wrestling promotion, but where they really excel is brawls, scuffles, and brouhahas . The latest commotion occurred on Thursday at the RAF 14 pre-fight press conference. Predictably, the chaos was centered around jiu-jitsu black belt and frequent nuisance Dillon Danis , who really has no other reason to be on a wrestling mat but to cause trouble. Danis unveiled his shirt that read “Khamzat is my b—ch” at the presser. When Khamzat Chimaev and Dillon Danis actually went head-to-head at RAF 10, “Borz” pinned him in 44 seconds , so the shirt doesn’t make much sense. Still, it was enough to send notorious hothead Arman Tsarukyan apoplectic, and the top-ranked Lightweight went ballistic in defense of his close friend and training partner (see all that here) . Where was Khamzat himself during all the chaos? New footage reveals that Chimaev was being restrained by about four people who appear to be a mix of RAF staff and civilians! “Borz” was desperate to get a piece of Danis and yelled out, “You don’t know who is your daddy b—ch! I’ll f—k you up!” Check it out: Khamzat Chimaev was PISSED at Dillon Danis 😳 "Hey you don't know who is your daddy b*tch! I'll f*ck you up." (via @RedCorner_MMA ) https://t.co/VRT1UFZCDU pic.twitter.com/uwdKVtCVot — Championship Rounds (@ChampRDS) October 22, 2026 While Danis and Tsarukyan will wrestle (and then probably brawl again) in the RAF 14 main event, Chimaev is also booked to compete. In the co-main event, he’ll take on former UFC Welterweight champion Robbie Lawler in a strange matchup that would seem to guarantee another dominant victory for the Russian. How about a little more challenge and a little more chaos? For the complete RAF 14 fight card and latest updates, click here .

item.title: Standout Stats | Juventus-Stade Rennais
item.description: Standout Stats | Juventus-Stade Rennais The Men's First Team drew 2-2 with Stade Rennais on Matchday 3 of the UEFA Europa League, as Zeki Celik and Nick Woltemade found the net at the Allianz Stadium. Let's take a look at some of the stats from the League Phase action. JUVENTUS-STADE RENNAIS STANDOUT STATS Nick Woltemade is only the third player to score in each of his first three appearances for Juventus in major European competitions, following Darko Kovačević in 1999 and Roberto Baggio in 1990. Juventus have scored at least nine goals in their first three matches of a major European competition for the first time since the 1999/00 season, when they netted 13 goals in the UEFA Cup. Zeki Çelik has scored two goals in nine appearances this season—matching the total he managed across 151 matches in all competitions during his previous spell at Roma. Juventus remain unbeaten at home in the UEFA Europa League, going 15 home games without defeat (W6 D9) – only Benfica have played more matches in the competition without losing a home game (30). Zeki Çelik's goal, coming after 4 minutes and 58 seconds, was the fastest scored by Juventus in the Europa League since Angel Di María's goal against Nantes after 4 minutes and 10 seconds on February 23, 2023. item.title: Here’s why Leipzig fans booed Real Madrid defender at the Bernabeu despite never facing him before
item.description: Here’s why Leipzig fans booed Real Madrid defender at the Bernabeu despite never facing him before Marc Cucurella was greeted with a standing ovation from Real Madrid supporters but also with a chorus of boos from RB Leipzig fans when he came on during the 4-1 victory over the German side . The reaction appeared puzzling because the Spanish defender had never faced Leipzig before, but the hostility can be traced back to Spain’s controversial Euro 2024 quarter-final against Germany. Notably, Cucurella replaced Carreras in the 70th minute, drawing applause from the home crowd at the Bernabeu. Leipzig’s travelling supporters, however, responded differently, reviving memories of an incident that remains contentious among German football fans. Cucurella’s Euro 2024 handball incident explains the boos The hostility dates back to the European Championship quarter-final between Spain and Germany, played on German soil in 2024. Spain won 2-1 to reach the semi-finals, but one incident involving Cucurella became a major talking point. During the match, Germany appealed for a penalty after a shot from Toni Kroos struck Cucurella’s arm inside the penalty area. The referee did not award a spot-kick, leaving German players and supporters frustrated with the decision. The incident became one of the defining controversies of Spain’s run through the tournament. Marc Cucurella was booed by the Leipzig fans. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Although Spain ultimately went on to win the European Championship, the disputed penalty appeal remained a source of anger among some German supporters. Leipzig supporters revive Germany’s frustration at the Bernabeu Cucurella’s appearance against Leipzig offered a reminder that the controversy had not been forgotten by everyone. The boos from the away section suggested that some German fans still associate the defender with the quarter-final decision, despite his having no previous history against the Bundesliga club. The reaction at the Bernabeu therefore had little to do with the Real Madrid-Leipzig contest itself. Instead, it showed lingering frustration from an international match played more than two years earlier.

item.title: Dayot Upamecano lauds Bayern Munich teammate Harry Kane
item.description: (Photo by Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images Harry Kane continues to make his case as one of the best players in world football, and his latest performance against Arsenal has earned him high praise from his Bayern Munich teammate, Dayot Upamecano. Kane recorded a g oal and an assist in Bayern’s 2-2 draw against the Gunners, once again demonstrating his importance to Vincent Kompany ’s side. Whether finishing chances himself or creating opportunities for his teammates, the England captain remains central to Bayern’s attacking th reat. Upamecano was particularly emphatic when discussing Kane’s quality, expressing his hope that the striker will eventually receive footba ll’s most prestigious individual award. “Harry is Harry. Outstanding. I hope he wins the Ballon d’O r,” Upamecano told Sky Germany’s Kerry Hau (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). It is a simple statement, but one that reflects the admiration Kane has earned within the Bayern dressing room. His goalscoring numbers, creativity, and ability to influence major matches make him a compe lling candidate for individual recognition. Ultimately, winning the Ballon d’Or will depend on sustained performances and team suc cess throughout the season. However, if Kane continues delivering against Europe’s biggest clubs, he will give hi mself every opportunity to enter that conversation. Join the conversation! item.title: Preview | Juventus Women-Roma
item.description: Preview | Juventus Women-Roma The Women's First Team are back in Serie A Women action, this time with a Matchday 4 clash against Roma at home. Let’s get up to speed ahead of Saturday's game with some pre-match stats. Interesting Facts Juventus have 21 wins to Roma's eight. Four draws complete the picture, including two in a final that ultimately awarded a trophy each. Juventus have scored 68 goals against Roma in all competitions, at least three more than against any other opponent in their history. Juventus leads the way in this season's opening season for both pass completion percentage (87.6%) and average ball possession (67.4%). Remina Chiba, along with Agnese Bonfantini, is one of two players who have scored more than one goal from the bench in the first three matchdays of this season's Serie A: two each. Annamaria Serturini played 156 games and scored 41 goals in all competitions for Roma between 2018 and 2024. The 1998-born player has already found the net against her former team in Serie A, scoring for Inter in January 2025. Gallery | Women | Roma up next for the Bianconere Opposition Focus Gianpiero Piovani has faced Juventus 22 times as a coach in Serie A, with Brescia, Sassuolo, and Inter; the current Roma coach has recorded five wins, four draws, and 13 defeats, and is unbeaten in his four most recent matches (3W, 1D). Roma, along with Inter and Como 1907, are one of three teams with a perfect record in the newly opened championship and could achieve four wins in their first four Serie A games of the season for the third time in their history - the previous two came in the 2023/24 and 2025/26 seasons. With one appearance, Manuela Giugliano will become the first player to reach the milestone of 150 Serie A appearances for Roma (149 currently).

item.title: Arizona women’s basketball puts up offensive avalanche in exhibition win over Embry-Riddle
item.description: Arizona men’s basketball had already played two exhibitions. Now it was the women’s turn. The Wildcats took on Embry-Riddle (Ariz.) and started the preseason off with a 117-44 blowout win over the Eagles. Arizona’s ability to get out in transition and turn defense into offense put the game out of reach very early. In Becky Burke ’s eyes, the exhibition had a lot of good but still had some bad. Overall, it’s all a learning experience. “We got exactly what we wanted out of this game,” said Burke. “We’re going to get a lot of great film overall. A lot of bright spots for us as well. We got to play a lot of people a lot of minutes. We got to score almost 120 points. So there’s a lot to be excited about, and there’s a lot to go back and watch and fix.” The Wildcats had six double figure scorers, led by a 22/11 double-double performance by Maryland transfer Breanna Williams and a 18 point performance by freshman Jasleen Green . The freshman was part of a starting lineup that included returners Sumayah Sugapong and Molly Ladwig , and transfers Aliyahnna “Puff” Morris and Gerda Raulušaityte . About five seconds into the game, Green got the scoring started for Arizona with her first bucket as a Wildcat in the form of an and-one. Morris followed with back-to-back layups as the Wildcats got out in transition quickly. “Coach Burke gives me a green light to go attack downhill, and that’s what we work on, so I’m used to that,” said Green. “I’ve never played in a crowd bigger than like 200 people. So playing in that atmosphere, getting an and-one for my first bucket, that was amazing.” Sugapong picked up right where she left off last season with a steal and score. Williams checked in early for Raulušaityte and set the tone for her night. Getting an offensive rebound off a missed free throw and after two more rebounds off her misses, she got her first points of the night. Makayla Presser-Palmer and Arynn “Simba” Finley also checked in early but even with the early rotation of players, there was no drop off in offensive production. A 21-4 lead for the Wildcats was just the start of their offensive explosion. “We wanted them to feel our pressure defensively,” said Burke. “We wanted them to feel us putting pressure on them on the defensive end in transition. I do feel like we achieved that tonight. We’re going to be a really gritty, aggressive, and deep group this year. We’re going to be able to keep fresh bodies and fresh legs in. The Wildcats took on Embry-Riddle (Ariz.) and started the preseason off with a 117-44 blowout win over the Eagles. Arizona’s ability to get out in transition and turn defense into offense put the game out of reach very early. In Becky Burke ’s eyes, the exhibition had a lot of good but still had some bad. Overall, it’s all a learning experience. “We got exactly what we wanted out of this game,” said Burke. “We’re going to get a lot of great film overall. A lot of bright spots for us as well. We got to play a lot of people a lot of minutes. We got to score almost 120 points. So there’s a lot to be excited about, and there’s a lot to go back and watch and fix.” The Wildcats had six double figure scorers, led by a 22/11 double-double performance by Maryland transfer Breanna Williams and a 18 point performance by freshman Jasleen Green . The freshman was part of a starting lineup that included returners Sumayah Sugapong and Molly Ladwig , and transfers Aliyahnna “Puff” Morris and Gerda Raulušaityte . About five seconds into the game, Green got the scoring started for Arizona with her first bucket as a Wildcat in the form of an and-one. Morris followed with back-to-back layups as the Wildcats got out in transition quickly. “Coach Burke gives me a green light to go attack downhill, and that’s what we work on, so I’m used to that,” said Green. “I’ve never played in a crowd bigger than like 200 people. So playing in that atmosphere, getting an and-one for my first bucket, that was amazing.” Sugapong picked up right where she left off last season with a steal and score. Williams checked in early for Raulušaityte and set the tone for her night. Getting an offensive rebound off a missed free throw and after two more rebounds off her misses, she got her first points of the night. Makayla Presser-Palmer and Arynn “Simba” Finley also checked in early but even with the early rotation of players, there was no drop off in offensive production. A 21-4 lead for the Wildcats was just the start of their offensive explosion. “We wanted them to feel our pressure defensively,” said Burke. “We wanted them to feel us putting pressure on them on the defensive end in transition. I do feel like we achieved that tonight. We’re going to be a really gritty, aggressive, and deep group this year. We’re going to be able to keep fresh bodies and fresh legs in. That’s not something we had the luxury to do last year.” In between Arizona going up and down the court in the first quarter, there came a point of confusion and surprise. Karolina Ulan checked into the game and so did a mystery player donning the number 52. Turns out Arizona had added Kent State transfer Dionna Gray to the team without an official announcement. Back in September, Gray was granted a fifth year of eligibility from a court in Indiana, and had joined the Wildcats only a week ago. “She was granted her year of eligibility, her fifth year of eligibility,” said Burke. “When that happened, obviously she was coached by Coach [Todd] Starkey at Kent State. When she got her year of eligibility and said she had some interest in coming to Arizona and just kind of giving us some depth, I knew exactly what she brings to the table. She’s a little jitterbug. She’s got a defensive mindset. She’s a veteran.” The following WBB players are eligible for the upcoming season per an Indiana court ruling today: Anala Nelson Catherine Alben Dionna Gray Jenna Van Schaik Maddy Skorupski Mia Nicastro Mya Petticord Some names here that can greatly impact a team this season. https://t.co/gzDWw0sdX3 — Skim Milkey (@SkimMilkey) September 23, 2026 After Ulan got a quick and-one, in came freshman Priyanka Ponnam . It felt like every time a new Wildcat stepped on the court they immediately put the ball in the basket. Ponnman came in and drilled a three with Sugapong following with one of her own. At the end of the first quarter, the Wildcats had put up 40 points while only allowing 13 on the other end. Arizona shot 72.7 percent from the field but that efficiency did not flow into the second quarter. Arizona had made it a priority to get the ball inside and score in the paint. Embry-Riddle was able to adjust to it and made it hard for the Wildcats to find success offensively. Callie Hinder was the last Wildcat to check in and at that point all available players had seen the court. In between the seven minute mark and four minute mark of the second quarter Sugapong had picked up three fouls, a trend that seems to have followed her from last season. The game flow had slowed down and after scoring 40 in the first quarter, Arizona only put up 18 more points in the second quarter. However, the second quarter would turn out to be the worst quarter of the game as both second-half quarters featured a good amount of offense. Raulušaityte found the scoreboard for the first time to start the second half. With Green scoring in double digits in the first half, she started a trend that five other players followed. Morris was the second Wildcat to reach double figures, with Williams securing her double-double early in the third and becoming the third player to score double digit points. “Bree’s come to life the last three weeks or so,” said Burke. “I think she battled a couple injuries early in the summer and was kind of in and out and has really worked herself into great shape and has been, over the last three weeks, the person that I brought her here to be. She should be a double-double every night for us.” “I feel like it’s a great debut,” said Williams. “It’s great playing in front of all those people in McKale. My teammates helped me do that, so I give credit to them as well.” Sugapong’s foul trouble did not stop as she picked up her fourth foul in the third. The good news for her is that her teammates did not allow any type of drop off when she was not on the court. Ulan’s third quarter burst helped grow the Arizona lead. She put 11 points of her own on the scoreboard and became the fourth Wildcat to get to double figures. Arizona put up 30 points in the third with a defensive dominant quarter only allowing six points. Sugapong came back on to the court in the fourth quarter and was the fifth player to get to double digits. Unfortunately for Sugapong, her fifth foul came on the following play and her night was done with 11 points. “I don’t really say too much to her when she fouls out or when she gets in foul trouble because you don’t want to put reins on that kid and try to reel her in and hold her back because at the same time she also led the the Big 12 in steals last year,” said Burke. “So she’s really aggressive at times, and it’s going to help you. She’s going to make game-winning plays, and then she’s really silly sometimes. She knows what she needs to do.” After a three pointer off a cross court pass from Gray, a transition bucket got Finley into double figures to make her the sixth and final player to reach that mark. Reaching the 100 point threshold was the final check point of the night for Arizona as it went on to secure the win. Arizona had only hit the 100 point mark once last season, and after losing last season’s opening exhibition, it was a complete turn around for Burke a year later. She hopes it’s a trend that continues as her second season in Tucson moves forward. “I think you’re gonna see me a lot happier up here on the podium this year, whatever the results are because of this group,” said Burke. “They’ve been a joy to coach. They’re so coachable. They’re so competitive. They’re so together and connected. They all want to be here.” Burke’s squad finished shooting 55.6 percent overall and went 32-42 from the free throw line. Arizona forced 31 turnovers and scored 34 points off of them. The Wildcats had 70 points in the paint, 20 second chance points, 47 fast break points, and 70 points from the bench. Arizona out

item.title: Bruins Postgame: DiPietro’s First Shutout Means So Much More
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Boston Bruins had plenty to celebrate on Thursday night, but Michael DiPietro ’s night meant much more than two points. The Bruins (8-2-1) extended their point streak to seven games with a commanding 6-0 win over the Nashville Predators (3-3-3) at TD Garden. Five different players scored, with David Pastrnak scoring twice and Casey Mittelstadt , Elias Lindholm , JJ Peterka , and Mark Kastelic adding one. Charlie McAvoy finished with four assists, and DiPietro made 28 saves in his first NHL shutout. Also Read: Bruins Roll Past Predators, Extend Point Streak to Seven Games The Bruins hosted Hockey Fights Cancer night on Thursday. DiPietro lost his mother to cancer when he was younger, making his first NHL shutout on Thursday all the more meaningful. “A little bit stressed out, but obviously, you couldn’t really write it better,” DiPietro said postgame. “For me, it means a lot on Hockey Fights Cancer night. My mom passed away when I was five from cancer. So for me, it means a lot, but also to my family and everyone back home, and I just want to make them proud, and obviously this is a really special moment.” DiPietro made stops on all 28 shots he faced, including seven high-danger shots. He finished with 3.78 goals saved above expected, according to Natural Stat Trick . After the game, the Bruins greeted their goaltender with a shower of water from their bottles. “I mean, what an awesome kid,” McAvoy, 28, said about DiPietro, 27. “Getting to know him last year through camp. And then this year, kind of knowing that he was going to have a spot on the team, which he earned. But man, all through camp, just some of the saves that he was making, just so impressive. Tonight to get his first shutout, you know, coming off the heels of his first win in Anaheim, it’s amazing.” DiPietro recorded his first NHL win last time out, and in his first start at home, recorded his first NHL shutout. He has played 100:17 without allowing a goal, with stops on each of his last 41 shots. “Of course, yeah. I think it starts creeping in your head,” DiPietro said when asked if the shutout was on his mind. “You’re on an island out there for a long time, so a bunch of thoughts come [to] your head. So I think just kind of acknowledging it, kind of moving on from it, and just trying to stay as present as possible and not trying to get too far ahead of yourself is important, and just kind of resetting after each whistle.” “The team had a great start. I just wanted to make sure that I was sharp whenever the pucks were coming.” After his first NHL win, Michael DiPietro said that he was not going to let the puck out of his sight. Marco Sturm harped on that after morning skate, but cited the Bruins coming out with “a good jump” on Thursday morning. That carried over into the game, as Casey Mittelstadt opened the scoring just 3:49 into the first period. The Bruins took a 2-0 lead into the first intermission and added two goals in every period, a much different response than their last return home. “You know what I liked the most, besides Mikey’s shutout, is that we came out with energy,” Sturm said after the game. “We talked about it in the morning. We addressed it. After a big road trip, it’s not always easy, but I thought it was one of the best pre-game skates we had all year. That’s exactly the way we skated – the energy, anything about it – we kind of carried it over to tonight’s game. And that’s where I’m happy with because now it shows for next time that we can do it. It’s just a mindset. Sometimes it’s hard, but that, for me, was the biggest reason why we won this game tonight.” The Bruins got off to a strong start and never wavered. They, like for much of the road trip, got contributions up and down their lineup. Five different Bruins found the back of the net, and they had two players with four-point nights. David Pastrnak, who had two goals and two assists on Thursday, now leads the team with six goals, but he’s one of seven players to have three or more tucks this season. “It’s amazing. Obviously it helps [that] every line is producing,” Pastrnak said. “It’s more like you’re waiting, just, ‘Who is it going to be tonight?’ So it’s fun to see. Every line is finding chemistry already, slowly. So we have good chemistry all around four lines, and it’s producing, so it’s good to see and makes it much easier for us defending and getting the wins.” “It’s been good. I think, especially when you kind of want to match lines or something,” JJ Peterka, another goal scorer on Thursday, added. “When every line is capable of scoring goals, every line is dangerous when they’re out there, and I think that’s a really nice thing to have.” The Bruins now have points in their last seven games, including a 6-3 win over the San Jose Sharks last Tuesday. They will close out their season series, and their brief two-game homestand, against the Sharks on Saturday night at 7:00 PM. item.title: Real Sociedad equal their record European away win at Lillestrøm as Sergio Gómez becomes their top Europa League scorer
item.description: Real Sociedad equal their record European away win at Lillestrøm as Sergio Gómez becomes their top Europa League scorer Real Sociedad won 6-0 in Norway to claim their first Europa League league-phase victory of the season, matching the biggest away win in their European history. Left-back Sergio Gómez scored twice and is now the club's top scorer in the competition ahead of Lyon's visit to Anoeta. The scoreline at Åråsen Stadion equalled the biggest away win in the club’s European history, according to Noticias de Gipuzkoa. The mark dates from a 6-0 win at Vardar on matchday three in 2017. UEFA described that game at the time as the biggest away win in Europa League history. Matarazzo’s side had struggled before Thursday. They lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth on matchday one. They then drew 1-1 away to Union SG on matchday two. Oyarzabal’s eight-minute spell settled the game early Lillestrøm had the better of the opening minutes and pressed the visitors hard. Within eight minutes, Oyarzabal’s creativity then turned the match. Sergio Gómez struck in the 25th and 27th minutes. The first came with his left foot, the second with a delicate right-footed finish past Dahlberg. Luka Sučić added the third in the 33rd minute. The hosts had a chance to respond after the break. Thomas Lehne Olsen missed a penalty in the 50th minute. Orri Steinn Óskarsson made it four in the 64th minute from a Gonçalo Guedes assist. Sučić scored again in the 72nd. Arsen Zakharyan completed the rout in the 80th minute from Benat Turrientes’s pass. The figures point to a closer contest than the score. Expected goals finished 2.29 for Lillestrøm against 2.46 for Real Sociedad. The hosts had 14 shots to 16. The gap lay in accuracy: Real Sociedad put 8 shots on target, Lillestrøm 2. The visitors also had 56% of possession. For Lillestrøm, the defeat compounds a difficult start. They had lost 2-1 at home to Torreense and drawn 1-1 at Sparta Praha in their first two league-phase games. A left-back is now Real Sociedad’s top scorer in Europe No Real Sociedad player has scored more in this season’s competition than Sergio Gómez, whose opening European goal came in the defeat to Bournemouth. The data provider rated him 9.04, just ahead of Sučić on 9.02. Spain’s other Europa League side also won away on matchday three. Celta came from behind to beat Celtic 2-1 in Glasgow. Javi Rodríguez scored both of their goals. Real Sociedad return to LaLiga against Levante at Anoeta on Sunday 25 October. That matchday 10 fixture kicks off at 17:30. Later European dates include a trip to Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park on 26 November. Torreense come to San Sebastián on 10 December. The league phase ends away to Juventus on 28 January 2027. item.title: Wesley continues to draw interest in Premier League
item.description: Wesley continues to draw interest in Premier League Wesley is running, convincing, and attracting attention in the Premier League. The Brazilian winger is carving out an increasingly important role for himself at Roma, as confirmed by his excellent performance against Slovan Bratislava. His performances are not going unnoticed in England, where Manchester United and Arsenal are among the clubs interested in the player. In recent weeks, Newcastle had also been linked with the Giallorossi full-back. However, that prospect appears to have cooled. According to Football Insider , the Magpies have no intention of submitting an offer for the Brazilian, held back by two financial obstacles. The first concerns the investments already made by the English club, which spent £29.5 million this summer to acquire a right-back. The second is linked to Roma’s valuation, which is reportedly asking for between €50 and €60 million to let Wesley leave. Newcastle currently appears incapable of investing this sum. Then there’s the position of the Giallorossi, which has no intention of parting ways with the Brazilian in the January transfer window. This desire further complicates the plans of the English contenders and postpones any potential negotiations, at least for now.

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.description: With Michael Carrick’s future at Old Trafford a matter of some debate, we examine the credentials of those who could succeed him The German was of interest to Manchester City while Omar Berrada was part of the hierarchy on the other side of town. He is highly thought of and would come with an impressive CV for a 39-year-old, having taken charge of Bayern Munich and Germany. Nagelsmann is regarded as an innovator who is very demanding of his players and builds teams to press relentlessly, a concept not currently used at United, as Bruno Fernandes will testify . His spell with Germany was underwhelming, concluding with a 2026 World Cup last-32 defeat by Paraguay , and at Bayern – with an exceptional squad – he won the Bundesliga in his only full season and was sacked the following March with the team second and still in the Champions League. item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US at Nu Stadium on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage Concacaf on Thursday announced it has approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg against the United States on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of the capital of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. Continue reading...

item.title: Carrick joins Wilcox under the bus after Manchester United’s latest night in crisis | Max Rushden
item.description: Bruno Fernandes followed Lisandro Martínez in revolt after his team’s 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League You have to credit Manchester United. Your local rivals have turned the Premier League into an almost meaningless farce. We are questioning the validity of anything we’ve seen over the past 20 years; wondering how many goals Erling Haaland will get in the Championship. We are looking at the league table from second position down and wishing we’d invested in inflatable bananas a month ago. And yet here comes the Old Trafford machine: from players to the captain to the manager to the director of football, to the director of the director of football, to a minority owner who feels the UK is being “colonised by immigrants” , to debt-leveraging majority owners who take vast sums out of the club and are collectively saying hold my Ineos-sponsored high-performance wellness immune boost smoothie. Continue reading...

And yet here comes the Old Trafford machine: from players to the captain to the manager to the director of football, to the director of the director of football, to a minority owner who feels the UK is being “colonised by immigrants” , to debt-leveraging majority owners who take vast sums out of the club and are collectively saying hold my Ineos-sponsored high-performance wellness immune boost smoothie. Continue reading...

item.title: Bruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at Arsenal
item.description: Midfielder says there were a lot of tears as he said goodbye at St James’ Park but he is enjoying the remorselessness at his new club For Bruno Guimarães, it was a time to show his steeliness, to fix his eyes on the prize – even if he knew it would surely mean them welling up. And then some. It was a tumultuous summer for the Brazil midfielder. A fine World Cup on a personal level was marred by a crucial penalty miss in the last-16 loss against Norway . Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle. Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022 ? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours? Continue reading...

item.title: Nottingham Forest’s false start places early focus on Glasner and Delap
item.description: Austrian’s tactics need adapting to but Forest are in the bottom three and their owner is not the patient type Sitting 19th in the Premier League was not the plan for Nottingham Forest after the arrival of a highly acclaimed manager and a £45m striker to fuel their ambitions. The fates of Oliver Glasner and Liam Delap are intertwined and with the stark stats of zero home goals and a solitary point at the City Ground it is not the dream start they were aiming for. As Delap prepares to return to Ipswich, where his career ignited, on Friday night, Forest are remaining calm. There is a desperation to get away from the short-termism that caused so many problems; 12 months ago, they were on their third head coach of a disappointing season. This summer they were ruthless with the removal of Vítor Pereira, who had done a fine job to escape the drop, because they saw an opportunity to upgrade with Glasner, hoping he could transform Forest like he did Crystal Palace. Continue reading...

item.description: Norwegian forward might look to Harry Kane for inspiration on the pitch, but when north London derby comes around, she needs no lessons on what the rivalry means “It means more than just three points. It’s for the whole club. It’s for the whole place. It’s for the whole of Tottenham.” One only needs to be in the presence of Tottenham Hotspur’s Cathinka Tandberg for a few minutes to feel the passion that emanates from her when it comes to this weekend’s north London derby. As a lifelong Spurs fan, the forward understands more than most the intensity of the rivalry that exists between her side and Arsenal, one that she cannot wait to experience once again on Saturday. “It will just be an incredible feeling,” she tells Moving the Goalposts. “I think you will feel a few nerves that you maybe don’t feel in a normal game but that’s good.” Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...
